item.title: Xinference CVE-2026-61539: RCE via unsafe eval() in Llama3 tool-call parsing
item.description: Added a tools page for the critical CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaw in Xinference (xorbitsai/inference, PyPI xinference), published to the GitHub Advisory Database on August 21, 2026 as CVE-2026-61539 / GHSA-x2rj-828p-hx9m. Affected versions (<= 2.5.0) parsed Llama3 model-generated tool-call output with Python eval(model_output, {}, {}) in xinference/model/llm/tool_parsers/llama3_tool_parser.py::extract_tool_calls(), so an attacker who can influence LLM output via the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions API (direct chat input or prompt injection) can execute arbitrary Python in the server process; in the tested default deployment the API required no authentication (CWE-95 eval injection; CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H). Fixed in 2.7.0 (fix PR #4786 merged 2026-04-14, PyPI release 2026-04-25), so the August advisory retroactively credits the disclosure of an April 2026 fix. No in-the-wild exploitation or actor attribution is reported. Distinct from the April 2026 TeamPCP-attributed supply-chain compromise of the same package (malicious 2.6.0-2.6.2 releases).

item.title: JSONata arbitrary-code-execution trio (CVE-2026-77413 / -77414 / -77415)
item.description: Added a tools page for the three critical JSONata (npm, ~1.65M downloads/week) arbitrary-code-execution advisories published to the GitHub Advisory Database on August 21, 2026 with public PoCs: CVE-2026-77413 (GHSA-8gq3-vp5j-2grp, missing hasOwnProperty check in the lookup function in src/functions.js, fixed by PR #794 in 2.2.0 and backported to 1.8.8), CVE-2026-77414 (GHSA-2943-5xfg-gq5f, bypassable hasOwnProperty check in environment.lookup in src/jsonata.js via $hasOwnProperty := $spread($string); $__proto__ := $constructor;, fixed by PR #799 in 2.2.1 and backported to 1.8.8), and CVE-2026-77415 (GHSA-66mm-25pp-rfff, chain of $clone overwrite mutating objects via evaluateTransformExpression, JSONata lambda destructuring such as $merge.*, and applyProcedure using proc.arguments.forEach instead of Array.prototype.forEach, fixed by PRs #799/#800/#802 in 2.2.1 and backported to 1.8.8). All three reach the same host primitive — recovering the host Function constructor from a crafted expression and executing child_process.execSync in the Node process — so any host that evaluates attacker-influenced JSONata expressions on jsonata < 2.2.1 / < 1.8.8 is a code-injection surface. Patch targets: jsonata ≥ 2.2.2 (latest) or ≥ 1.8.9 (latest-v1). All three are CWE-94, critical; no in-the-wild exploitation or actor attribution is reported.

item.title: isolated-vm ExternalCopy type-confusion sandbox escape (GHSA-864f-rcv7-6rh4)
item.description: Added a tools page from Endor Labs' August 20, 2026 writeup (Cris Staicu) of a critical type-confusion flaw in isolated-vm (npm, 1M+ downloads/week), the V8-based sandbox used by n8n, Activepieces, Mastra, Sim.ai, Budibase, Directus, and Rocket.Chat to run model- and user-generated JavaScript. The flaw sits in the host-to-sandbox data handoff, ivm.ExternalCopy(value, {transferList}), in src/external_copy/serializer.cc: the transfer_list JS array is walked twice, first validating each element with IsArrayBuffer() and then performing an unchecked As<ArrayBuffer>() reinterpret-cast. Because the list is read through array->Get(context, index), a stateful index-getter can return a real ArrayBuffer on walk 1 (passing validation) and a different value such as the integer 0x41414141 on walk 2, corrupting a V8 object handle. A guest needs only a single ivm.Reference to recover the ExternalCopy constructor, so the primitive is reachable with the default handoff. Steering the confused object into a JS string makes the attacker control which bytes are read as an object's fields, and Transfer's destruction path ends in an indirect call through a vtable pointer read from that memory. Endor Labs demonstrated a PoC that recovers the host ASLR base, forges a fake control block and vtable in sprayed heap, and drives the indirect call to a chosen libc function (guest-to-host RCE, not just a crash); the full exploit was shared privately with the maintainer. Fixed in isolated-vm 7.0.1 and 6.2.0 (published 2026-08-05 / 2026-08-06) by wrapping ExternalCopy::Copy in v8::Isolate::DisallowJavascriptExecutionScope; GHSA-864f-rcv7-6rh4 was published 2026-08-07 (critical), CVE pending, no in-the-wild exploitation reported. The page documents the affected/patched version matrix, upgrade and detection notes, and assessment limits.

item.title: Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-19489 / CVE-2026-19490 Gateway/AAA auth bypass and LSN/SIP-ALG DoS
item.description: Added Citrix's August 20, 2026 NetScaler ADC / Gateway update covering two customer-managed flaws. CVE-2026-19490 (CVSS 9.3) is an authentication bypass on appliances configured as a Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN, RDP Proxy) or AAA virtual server, gated on version-specific SAML-action preconditions; CVE-2026-19489 (CVSS 8.8) is a memory overflow / DoS only when SIP ALG is enabled on a Large Scale NAT group. No in-the-wild exploitation was reported; credited to a JPMorgan Chase pen-tester. Fixed in 14.1-73.32, 13.1-63.21, 14.1-73.32 FIPS, and 13.1-37.277 (or later) as applicable. Citrix-managed cloud services and Adaptive Authentication are already updated. Page documents per-version applicability, Citrix's published precondition greps, NetScaler Console Global Deny Lists mitigation, and patch-now / exposure-measurement defender heuristics for internet-facing remote-access front doors.

item.title: LLM-slop false CVEs: AI-generated SQLite advisory batch poisoning NVD / CISA
item.description: Added a durable pattern page from JFrog Security Research's July 30, 2026 "SQLite Critical CVEs or LLM Slop?" analysis. A newly created GitHub repository (programmervuln/cveadvisory-) published a batch of SQLite vulnerability advisories plus 50+ other CVEs that NVD flagged critical and CISA ADP agreed with. JFrog's isolated ASan-instrumented verification found the cited functions do not exist in the claimed versions, the claimed 3.51.2-to-3.51.3 "patch" made zero changes to src/expr.c, the PoCs do not crash, none of the CVEs appear on SQLite's official advisory page, and the advisories flag as AI-generated under GPTZero. Red Hat initially scored CVE-2026-51302 10.0 Critical before downgrading to 7.6. The page treats the vulnerability data pipeline itself as an attack surface and records heuristics: verify against the vendor advisory page first, disqualify non-existent code references, distrust inherited severity, PoC-verify before emergency patching, and gate automated patching behind provenance checks.

item.title: UAT-10147: SPECTRE, BadIIS, and agentic-AI-augmented web-server intrusions
item.description: Added Cisco Talos' paired August 20, 2026 reports (Joey Chen) documenting UAT-10147, a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking intrusion actor targeting internet-exposed Windows (IIS) and Linux (Nginx/Apache-style) web servers worldwide, monetized through SEO fraud (the BadIIS malware-as-a-service and a C# ASHX SeoEngineHandler targeting the Coc Coc crawler) and data theft. The campaign was exposed when the download server 139.180.197[.]150 ran an open directory listing, revealing a target list of roughly 170,000 URLs split across 17 files (~10,000 each, "w" = 万). Documented initial-access CVEs include CVE-2022-27925 (Zimbra), CVE-2021-23758 (AjaxPro), CVE-2021-29441/29442 (Nacos), CVE-2019-18935 (Telerik), CVE-2022-0995 (watch_queue), CVE-2021-3156 (Baron Samedit), CVE-2015-5287 (ABRT), CVE-2015-3246 (libuser), CVE-2010-3904 (RDS), and CVE-2022-0847 (Dirty Pipe), with C2 infrastructure on vn[.]xyz (SeoEngineHandler) and adminapi.tippusoni[.]in (BadIIS downloads). Recovered artifacts show agentic-AI integration into post-compromise operations: DeepAudit and PentestGPT traces, ysoserial ViewState tooling, an AI-generated ASP.NET ViewState RCE "guide" with four companion Python scripts (check_paths, deploy_implant, deploy_shell, exfil), and AI-assisted exploit refinement and troubleshooting. Observed victims span Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada, and Vietnam across government, education, media, tech, and gaming sectors.

item.title: SPECTRE (cross-platform C backdoor) and the Specter Linux rootkit
item.description: Added Cisco Talos' analysis of SPECTRE, a new cross-platform C backdoor tracked in UAT-10147 activity, named from a recovered debug-log sample whose header explicitly read "SPECTRE." The Windows variant implements 45 C2 commands; the Linux variant implements 29. Both provide cross-platform C2, three injection modalities, credential theft, and weighted anti-analysis scoring. The Linux SPECTRE binary loads the Specter kernel rootkit, which masquerades as acpi_pad.ko behind a hardware-monitor.service systemd unit ordered Before=sysinit.target and hooks syscalls via ftrace IPMODIFY with a magic PID 31337, blinding user-level security tooling. The Windows variant pairs with a BYOVD EDR-killer using CVE-2019-16098 (RTCore64.sys) or CVE-2021-21551 (DBUtil_2_3.sys) to unlink PspCreateProcess/PspCreateThread/PssCallProcessNotifyRoutine and image-load callbacks, killing kernel-callback-based EDR. Talos assessed with medium confidence that portions of the Specter rootkit and the custom-compiled Potato tools were developed with AI-assisted code generation.

item.title: BTR Reforged: weaponizing Defender's BTR.sys remediation driver as a kernel primitive
item.description: Added Check Point Research's August 20, 2026 publication by Jiří Vinopal (presented at Black Hat USA 2026 / DEF CON 34) — the first full reverse engineering of BTR.sys, the legitimate Microsoft-signed Windows Defender Boot Time Removal driver embedded in MpEngine.dll as the BOOTTIMETOOL resource. BTR_CLI constructs valid RC4-encrypted transactions (hard-coded 256-byte key in .rdata, modified CRC-32 integrity, config carried in a :changelist ADS stream) and installs the driver as a Boot Bus Extender service, yielding arbitrary Ring 0 file and registry operations on Windows 7 through Windows 11 25H2 with no vulnerability, no memory corruption, and no external driver import. Because BTR.sys is a required Windows component it cannot be blocked via the Vulnerable Driver Blocklist or WDAC without breaking Defender, and the PoC deliberately mimics legitimate remediation telemetry, so detection is behavioral (randomized driver filename + transient service + ADS config + RC4 + self-cleanup at boot). No in-the-wild abuse was observed; the technique is positioned as a BYOVD-alternative EDR/AV bypass and as the same "Defender's own components are the attack surface" threat model as RoguePlanet/ShieldBreak (CVE-2026-50656).

item.title: Broadcom/Spring August 2026 security advisory: 91 CVEs and the AI vulnerability-consumption gap
item.description: Added Sonatype Research's August 21, 2026 analysis of Broadcom's August 20, 2026 Spring security-advisory batch, which Sonatype tracked as 91 CVEs across Spring Framework and related projects (Spring Security, Spring Cloud Config, Spring AI, Spring Data REST, Spring Integration, Reactor Core, Reactor Netty, Spring AMQP, Spring Batch). Sonatype Guide identified 209,569 affected components at publication, many non-Spring components bundling vulnerable Spring code. Two standouts: CVE-2026-59285, an unsafe-deserialization flaw in Spring for GraphQL (CVSS 9.2 Critical, exploitable with Jackson 2.x, paginated GraphQL fields, and abusable classes), and CVE-2026-59318, a Spring AI tool-calling request-boundary bypass where prompt injection can invoke a tool not made available to the current request (privilege escalation; prompt-level restrictions are not enforced controls). Context: Spring's report intake jumped from a ~6.5/month historical baseline to 55 in March 2026 and 482 across 65 projects in April 2026, with Broadcom reporting a 1,700% increase in monthly advisories and its June 2026 release the largest in the project's 23-year history; Sonatype frames this as the AI vulnerability-consumption problem (AI-assisted discovery outpacing downstream remediation). No Spring CVEs were in CISA KEV at the catalog's 2026.08.21 release; monitor for additions, especially CVE-2026-59285. Defender priorities: inventory Spring exposure by direct/transitive dependency, prioritize by actual exposure and exploitability, enforce AI tool availability at the system level rather than only in model instructions, and plan for recurring large-batch disclosures.

item.title: RedC2 4.0 (RedShell Linux beacon) and the trojanized-npm delivery wave
item.description: Added TrendAI's analysis (reported via The Hacker News August 21, 2026) of RedC2 4.0, a cross-platform C2 framework sold for $99.99 via the Red Offsec clearnet site and advertised on Hack Forums by "MarlboroMan" (v2.0 Aug 2025, v3.0 Jan 2026, v4.0 Jun 2026). Fourteen trojanized npm packages (streak-metrics-math, kit-map-vim, streak-map-cache, streak-map-kit, map-streak-kit, streak-cache-map, streak-calc-metrics, streak-calc-math, streak-math-abz, streak-metricsaz, streak-math-metrics, streak-metricazbd, streak-metricsazb, streak-kit-map, all at 1.0.0/1.0.1) masquerade as functional calendar/streak utilities; their dist/index.mjs entry files re-export genuine date helpers and launch a bundled "native math accelerator" binary (math-core.bin, math-calc.bin, calc-math.dat, etc.) that drops the RedShell Linux beacon — with no install hook, a single import anywhere in the dependency graph is enough to execute. RedShell provides /bin/sh-backed interactive commands (SSH-key and browser-credential collection, in-memory ELF execution, SOCKS5 proxying, pivoting), and RedC2 4.0 ships Red Agent, an LLM-backed command-execution layer that turns natural-language post-exploitation intent into beacon commands. Coverage records the 14-package IOC set, import-time (not install-time) execution mechanics, defender priorities (registry/lockfile blocks, node_modules native-binary watches, RedShell behavior hunts, Red Offsec/actor tracking), and assessment limits (no victim or actor attribution; 14 packages are the identified set, not necessarily the full set).

item.title: Zimbra SNMP command injection in CISA KEV; Microsoft patches Entra ID deserialization flaw (August 21, 2026)
item.description: CISA added Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) CVE-2026-73570 (CVSS 8.9, CWE-78) to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 21, 2026 with a 2026-08-24 BOD 26-04 deadline: an OS command injection in the optional zimbra-snmp monitoring component, unauthenticated via crafted SMTP requests when SNMP notifications are enabled, and a permanent fix for the critical SNMP vulnerability Zimbra disclosed June 26, 2026 in Zimbra 10.1.20 (July 20, 2026). Active exploitation was reported by CERT Polska via The Hacker News on August 20, 2026, with /var/log/zimbra.log restart artifacts and /opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps file-plant hunts. The same day, Microsoft patched Microsoft Entra ID CVE-2026-69836 (CVSS 10.0, CWE-502 deserialization RCE, discovered by Robert Fitzpatrick); Microsoft's bulletin first marked the Exploited field "Yes" ("already been fully mitigated") then corrected it to "No" ("not exploited in the wild") after The Hacker News contacted the company, and as of the catalog's 2026.08.21 release CVE-2026-69836 is not in KEV. Coverage records the disputed exploitation status, defender priorities (patch SNMP-enabled ZCS to 10.1.20 now; inventory on-prem/federated identity surfaces fronting Entra), and assessment limits, and notes no shared campaign is established between the two same-day events.

item.title: DoFun Android head-unit malware: MoYu/BADBOX ad-fraud and proxy botnet via TWCore updaters
item.description: Added Kaspersky's August 21, 2026 analysis (discovered June 2026) of the first documented malware infection chain specific to Android-based automotive head units running DoFun firmware (30M+ vehicle owners worldwide). Attackers abuse TWCore, the legitimate built-in software-update app, to push a UI-less Trojan dropper named JarService with no user interaction; it installs a multi-stage downloader that beacons to 144.217.243[.]201 (payload path /vr34der34/dex3.68.png, version-encoded names back to dex3.57) and deploys a background clicker that POSTs to /cpc/api/task every 90 minutes, driven by integer productId commands (http, web, copy, loadlib2, deeplink, traceroute) observed in use for ad-click fraud and residential-proxy botnet operation. The Hacker News attributes the activity with high confidence to the MoYu Group, the operator HUMAN Satori outed in 2025 behind the BADBOX ad-fraud/residential-proxy scheme that Google sued 25 unnamed Chinese individuals or entities over in July 2025. Coverage records the full chain, command set, attribution caveats, and defender priorities (fleet TWCore-update-channel audit, JarService and /cpc/api/task beacon hunts, treating infected head units as proxy/exit nodes).

item.title: Fake TradingView macOS stealer delivered by a paid YouTube ad
item.description: Added SafeDep's August 21, 2026 analysis of a macOS implant whose infection began with a paid Google video ad on YouTube impersonating TradingView, driving the victim to a fake .pkg installer. The implant is a remote-controlled task runner persisting through a self-healing LaunchAgent watchdog (com.microsoft.service.systemhelperwatcher.v8mgfk) that re-fetches a shell stager from Cloudflare-fronted velvetforge.net / cedarengine.com every five minutes. The stager runs a GET /script eval loop gated on launchd and a mislabeled application/pdf content type, authenticates with an X-Machine-Id header and a hard-coded HS256 JWT, and silently sudo-es via a plaintext password cached at /Users/Shared/.passwd. The payload is an 18.6 MB AES-256-CBC-encrypted V8 code cache (key 2e1ba69f…) loaded through a legitimate signed Node.js binary plus NODE_OPTIONS=--require, evading Gatekeeper; six 0.<hash>.node ncc modules add keylogging, ScreenCaptureKit and CGVirtualDisplay capture, keychain access, UI automation, and a local TLS-terminating MITM proxy on 127.0.0.1:49313 backed by a rogue root CA in the System keychain. Coverage records the full delivery chain, self-healing persistence semantics, decrypted payload mechanics, per-module capability detail, hunter commands, and the IOC set, and notes the inferred (not confirmed) WEEVILPROXY / JSCEAL lineage.

item.title: Russian auth-focused espionage: Google OAuth and WhatsApp device-link hijacking (GTIG)
item.description: Added Google Threat Intelligence's August 20, 2026 report on three suspected-Russian cyber-espionage clusters — UNC6293, UNC7005 (Storm-2945), and UNC5976 — that abuse legitimate authentication flows to compromise academia, aerospace/defense, government, and think-tank targets in Europe and the U.S. Coverage records UNC6293's small-scope diplomatic app-password and OAuth phishing, UNC7005's May–June 2026 WhatsApp device-linking spoofing that records audio/video and harvests credentials, its Vidar/Atomic(AMOS) infostealer use against U.S. targets, and its early-August 2026 Google OAuth phishing via FOC-spoofing domains; UNC5976's file-sharing-domain + Google-Cloud-project OAuth token harvesting and its HEADRUSH Excel-plugin HTA delivery. The report ties these operations to the CaptiveCrunch hospitality captive-portal campaign and to Lumen Black Lotus Labs' suspected MSP supply-chain compromise (~70 victim IPs). Defender guidance covers treating device-linking prompts as high-risk identity events, alerting on OAuth redirects to unverified Cloud projects, scoping device-code flows, and reviewing MSP-managed environments; attribution caveats (Google's assessment, not multi-agency confirmed) and the unconfirmed MSP-scope inference are preserved.

item.title: Wiz stage-2 implant analysis and DPRK infrastructure overlap in the arrayref Rust supply-chain attack
item.description: Updated the arrayref / proc-macro1 page with Wiz Research's August 20, 2026 write-up: a stage-2 implant recovered from Google Threat Intelligence samples (POST /49890878 beaconing, Chrome/Brave/Edge SQLite saved-login enumeration, kill/minicfg/startup/runscript commands, per-OS persistence via HKCU Run / LaunchAgent / systemd user service, DGA .com fallback, AES-128-GCM configuration under the hardcoded key "i am botking" with an embedded RSA-2048 private key, and the stage-2 SHA1 set) plus a DPRK-overlap assessment. The overlap is shared infrastructure, not operator attribution: the same /49890878 beacon path and 23.254.164.0/23 Hostwinds range as the Microsoft-attributed Mastra/Sapphire Sleet campaign, plus 23.254.167[.]216 appearing in GCTI's UNC1069 axios analysis. Coverage also adds Wiz's environment-prevalence figures (arrayref in over 35% of environments, ~75% of Rust-present ones) and its remediation additions.

item.title: CISA adds both Head Mare TrueConf flaws to KEV (CVE-2026-72529 / CVE-2026-72530)
item.description: Updated the Head Mare TrueConf / PhantomCore / PhantomGraph campaign page: CISA added both exploited flaws to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 20, 2026 — CVE-2026-72529 (TrueConf Server missing authentication for critical function, CWE-306; BOD 26-04 deadline August 23) and CVE-2026-72530 (TrueConf Server code injection, CWE-94; deadline September 3). The KEV entries confirm the unpatched-at-exploitation status of the 5.3.x-5.3.8 / 5.4.x-5.4.8 / 5.5.x-5.5.4 lines and close the earlier open KLCERT-26-057/058-to-CVE question; the June 18, 2026 5.3.9 / 5.4.9 / 5.5.5 fixes close both flaws.

item.title: Trusted collaboration-channel identity abuse
item.description: Added Unit 42's August 20, 2026 analysis of threat actors misusing enterprise collaboration platforms (Microsoft Teams, Slack, and similar) as the trusted channel for identity phishing, impersonation, credential theft, malware delivery, and social engineering. Unit 42's 12-month endpoint alerts of collaboration-tool-associated malicious activity more than quadrupled, and 99% relate to chat phishing: attackers operate inside an authenticated channel — a compromised account, external federated tenant, guest, or trusted third-party relationship — so malicious requests look routine. Coverage records the durable trust-transference pattern, the January 2026 Fireblocks recruitment-themed campaign (assessed aligned with the North Korea-linked Contagious Interview pattern), the March 2026 staged-Slack-workspace attack on the Axios npm maintainer that converted into two poisoned Axios registry releases, the April 2026 OpenSSF Linux Foundation TODO Group Slack campaign, the CERT Polska December 2025 appliance intrusion that exfiltrated privileged credentials and disabled 2FA through a native Slack-webhook integration, the MITRE mapping (T1566 / T1684.001 / T1556), and defender heuristics including external-federation and guest-allow-listing, post-authentication behavioral correlation, webhook-egress triage, out-of-band verification policy, and maintainer-targeting correlation. No single actor is asserted; the page is a cross-platform pattern alongside the Teams-specific external-chat phishing entry.

item.title: JFrog expands the Rust crate compromise: internment and append-only-vec join arrayref
item.description: Updated the arrayref / proc-macro1 Rust supply-chain page with JFrog Security Research's August 20, 2026 independent confirmation: two more parent crates in the same droundy owner account — internment 0.8.7 (~14.4M downloads) and append-only-vec 0.1.9 (~4.5M downloads) alongside arrayref 0.3.10 (~245M) — all silently pulling the proc-macro1 1.0.107 typosquat carrier whose build.rs carries the split-base64 C2, accept-all TLS, and detached stage-2 spawn. Coverage adds the JFrog Xray IDs (XRAY-1058266 through 1058269), clean-version pins (=0.3.9 / =0.8.6 / =0.1.8), per-OS stage-3 blob names, the spoofed David Tolnay author metadata corroborating the dtolney persona, and the caveat that the inactive 23.254.165.112:9089/:443 endpoints at JFrog's writing do not mean failed execution.

item.title: Rust supply-chain attack: arrayref 0.3.10 and the proc-macro1 typosquat execute a remote payload at build time
item.description: Added coverage of the August 20, 2026 Rust crates.io supply-chain incident: compromised arrayref 0.3.10 (published 07:15 UTC, first dependency in the crate's decade-long history) pulled in a typosquatted proc-macro1 crate (1.0.106 staging copy of proc-macro2, 1.0.107 payload) whose build.rs downloads a platform-specific stage-2 binary from 23.254.165.112:9089 (Hostwinds hwsrv-798836.hostwindsdns.com) and executes it detached from the Cargo build. The legitimate droundy maintainer account (in good standing since 2009) is presumed compromised; the attacker's dtolney persona impersonating David Tolnay was fabricated the same morning with forged rchaitm@gmail.com metadata. A scripted yank burst of arrayref 0.3.5-0.3.9 nudged lockfile holders toward the trap. Exposure window was roughly 86 minutes; reverse-dependency reach includes tiny-skia/winit (egui/eframe, iced), blake3, revm-precompile, and solana-runtime/spl-token. Coverage records the full UTC timeline, IOCs (files, binaries, hashes, network), lockfile-based triage, and CI hardening guidance. Stage-2 payload behavior is still under analysis per StepSecurity; no actor attribution asserted.

item.title: Elementor Pro CVE-2026-32475 unauthenticated RCE and WordPress 7.0.4 CVE-2026-65640
item.description: Added Patchstack-reported Elementor Pro CVE-2026-32475 (CVSS 9.0, unauthenticated remote-code-execution in the Forms module's File Upload field, patched in 4.2.2 on August 19, 2026) and WordPress core CVE-2026-65640 (CVSS 8.8, Author-or-higher RCE via malicious Postscript media handed to ImageMagick, fixed in WordPress 7.0.4 on August 12, 2026). Coverage records the Elementor dual-file-part extension-bypass mechanics and the predictable-shape wp-content/uploads/elementor/forms/<uniqid>.php upload sink, the forced-update nature of WordPress 7.0.4, defender priorities including emergency patching, Form-widget exposure inventory, WAF/extension blocklists, and post-exploitation web-shell hunts, and the assessment limits (no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation as of the survey).

item.title: Stealing reasoning traces: encrypted-reasoning replay across sessions, users, and models (arXiv:2608.09867)
item.description: Added coverage of the August 10, 2026 arXiv:2608.09867 paper ("Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs", Panfilov et al.) demonstrating that OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google's client-side encrypted reasoning blocks are interchangeable across sessions, users, and models within a provider. Using a weaker same-provider model as a fuzzy decoder, the authors built a scalable decryption jailbreak and documented four abuse paths: anti-distillation bypass, private-data extraction from public agent logs (6,708 trajectories / 315,320 decoded blocks / 367 PII + 182 credentials per the abstract; 704 artifacts per The Hacker News), hidden hazardous-content disclosure, and invisible prompt injection via replayed opaque blocks. Coverage records the mechanics, the August 2026 mitigations and reproducibility statement, and defender priorities for stripping reasoning blocks from logs, treating shared agent logs as PII/credential stores, and defending against invisible prompt injection in agentic workflows.

item.title: OpenAI pauses frontier RL training for two weeks amid expanded monitoring
item.description: Added an August 18, 2026 follow-up to the Hugging Face autonomous-agent production intrusion page: OpenAI published "Pacing model development in an era of cyber-critical capabilities," disclosing a two-week pause on reinforcement learning training for its latest frontier models while it "shored up additional defenses and increased the scope of its monitoring" to avert another Hugging Face-like incident. This operationalizes the August 7 Astra containment: the pause extends to training workloads on current frontier models, not just evaluation or partner activities, and the disclosure frames internal evaluation and training infrastructure as a live attack surface. The page now carries the full source set including the OpenAI post and The Hacker News summary.

item.title: Microsoft Defender CVE-2026-50656 RoguePlanet / ShieldBreak patch bypass leaves SYSTEM escalation open
item.description: Added Arctic Wolf Labs' August 12, 2026 report that researcher "Chaotic Eclipse" released ShieldBreak, a public exploit fully bypassing Microsoft's July 2026 initial patch (Engine 1.1.26060.3008) for CVE-2026-50656 (RoguePlanet), a race-condition-plus-link-resolution local privilege escalation in mpengine.dll that lets a low-privilege local user reach NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. No official fix for the ShieldBreak bypass was available as of the alert, so patched-and-current Defender environments remain exposed. Coverage records the exploit mechanics, defender actions including host-level mitigation, and the patch-bypass monitoring outlook.

item.title: Cloudflare Workers remote Spectre attack leaks co-tenant JWT at 12 bits/second
item.description: Added coverage of the arXiv:2608.17043 paper (TU Graz and collaborators) demonstrating a remote Spectre side-channel against production Cloudflare Workers that leaked a JSON Web Token from a co-located worker at up to 12 bits/second, roughly 360x faster than the 2021 remote-Spectre demonstration on the same platform. The end-to-end experiment used attacker- and researcher-controlled workers with no customer data accessed, and Cloudflare found no indicators of active exploitation over the preceding three years. Cloudflare states the attack is mitigated in production via improved Dynamic Process Isolation, V8 Sandbox integration, and MPK-based in-process isolation.

item.title: City Forum: single-IP Salesforce and ServiceNow guest-access scraping since March 2025
item.description: Added Reco's naming of the City Forum campaign: a single Contabo VPS (158.220.87.79) with the default Go net/http user agent has scraped records from both Salesforce and ServiceNow customer portals since at least March 2025, spanning telecoms, banks, financial services, enterprise software vendors, and public-sector portals. The root cause is a guest identity granted more access than the site needed to serve the public: Salesforce Experience Cloud guest profiles reaching Aura and Lightning Web Runtime UI-API objects, and ServiceNow Service Portal guests hitting the anonymous POST /api/now/sp/search endpoint. Reco has not attributed the campaign to a named group; it is distinguished from the widely reported ShinyHunters Salesforce abuse mainly by the range of surfaces it touches.

item.title: StubMaker: 16 typosquatted RubyGems packages deliver a Windows stealer
item.description: Added OpenSourceMalware's (with Paul "6mile" McCarty) StubMaker campaign tracking: sixteen clumsy typosquats of popular Ruby gems (r18n, i18n, active_support, builder-style names) published by RubyGems owner accounts mod8rz41mje and rbq95bwt6q between at least mid-August 2026, all delivering the same Windows information stealer for browser-credential and cryptocurrency-wallet theft via install-time execution. The durable finding is weaponization of RubyGems' yank-and-reclaim behavior: when all of a gem's versions are yanked, the name becomes claimable, letting the attacker re-publish malicious versions under previously dead package names. Discovered August 15, 2026; packages yanked.

item.title: Balonx Sistema: Mexican banking PhaaS with live sessions, Android RAT, and AI vishing
item.description: Added Group-IB's technical analysis of Balonx Sistema, a Mexican banking Phishing-as-a-Service platform targeting 20+ financial institutions with weekly subscription tiers (3,000/6,000 MXN), live WebSocket victim sessions with 14 on-demand fraudulent screens, an integrated Spyroid-based Android RAT, and a CallFlow AI synthetic-voice vishing module. Leaked GitHub repositories exposed the operations, victims, infrastructure, and affiliate network; the platform has harvested credentials and financial information from 1,100+ users since at least October 2025.

item.title: PATCHCORD / SHEETCORD: APT36 backdoor campaign against Afghan telecom and South Asian critical infrastructure
item.description: Added Acronis TRU's report of an ongoing campaign delivering the previously undocumented C/C++ PATCHCORD backdoor against Afghan telecom providers and South Asian critical-infrastructure organizations, with fake AFTEL VPN installer and telecom-management lures (Telecom_TMS.zip / TMS_AfghanTelecom.exe Inno Setup chain). A second Go-based backdoor, SHEETCORD, uses Google Sheets C2; a related domain impersonates India's National Informatics Centre. Moderate-confidence attribution to APT36 (Transparent Tribe) based on targeting, malware, infrastructure, and tradecraft overlap.

item.title: Unisoc VoLTE video-call exploit chain reaches full Android kernel access
item.description: Added coverage of SSD Secure Disclosure's August 17, 2026 publication of stage two of a two-part Unisoc modem-firmware exploit chain: after the March 2026 VoLTE SIP video-call RCE, a shared-resource isolation flaw (CWE-1189) escalates to full Android kernel access on T606/T612/T7250 SoCs (tested on Motorola E13, Realme C33, Xiaomi Redmi A5). Completing the chain requires an attacker-controlled private 4G network and a victim who answers the video call. No CVE assigned; Unisoc has not responded to repeated outreach.

item.title: Head Mare: TrueConf server exploitation delivers PhantomCore and PhantomGraph
item.description: Added Kaspersky Threat Response's August 11, 2026 report on a July 2026 Head Mare campaign that exploited two TrueConf server vulnerabilities (KLCERT-26-057 / KLCERT-26-058, affecting 5.3.x-5.5.5) to plant a web shell in locale.php, then replaced legitimate TrueConf client installers with PhantomCore carriers and deployed the PhantomGraph backdoor (SysExcSvc.dll / SysReadSvc.dll Windows services, Microsoft OneDrive C2) to video-conference participants. Head Mare is reclassified from hacktivist cluster to APT group; affected builds were patched June 18, 2026 in 5.3.9 / 5.4.9 / 5.5.5. Coverage records the attack chain, the CLSID InprocServer32 persistence key, and defender priorities including client-distribution integrity audits and OneDrive-C2 hunting.

item.title: CoolClient adds a signed kernel-mode rootkit driver (HoneyMyte / Mustang Panda)
item.description: Added Kaspersky GReAT's August 14, 2026 finding that the newest CoolClient variant used by the HoneyMyte APT group (also tracked as Mustang Panda) deploys a signed kernel-mode driver as a Windows service with dedicated IOCTL handlers that hide the CoolClient process, protect related files and registry entries, and block inspection or modification - an architecture comparable to ToneShell's kernel enhancements. Observed in intrusions across Pakistan, Mongolia, and Myanmar (late 2025-2026). The documented Myanmar intrusion shows Defender folder/file exclusions, a fake %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft\Windows Defender staging directory, a renamed Sangfor executable used as DLL sideloader, and SYSTEM persistence via a scheduled task named after the Windows Defender Advanced Threat Protection service.

item.title: Armored Likho Still Toolkit: Telegram session theft and audio eavesdropping in Russia
item.description: Added Kaspersky GReAT's August 13, 2026 report on a May 2026 Armored Likho (Eagle Werewolf) espionage campaign against Russian individuals and organizations in major corporations, the public sector, IT, and education. Initial access used a Rust/Tauri app mimicking a donation service (catalog fetched from orderapiserver[.]info) as a dropper. The new Still Toolkit suite includes Still Sync, a Tokio-based Rust stealer that steals Telegram tdata session files and pulls chat logs and media through the Telegram API (gRPC/FlatBuffers, default C2 tg4service[.]com:443), and Still Audio, a speech-detecting audio surveillance implant that uploads recordings to C2.

item.title: Project CAV3RN continues: Google Apps Script C2 relay and DNS-based channel selection
item.description: Updated the Cavern page with Kaspersky GReAT's August 11, 2026 "Project CAV3RN continues" report on the Iran-linked Cavern Manticore cluster. The new GoogleService.dll communication module selects C2 transport per transaction from DNS A-record responses: a direct HTTPS channel at api.studiotikva[.]com gated by an X-Client-Id header, or a Google Apps Script relay at script.google[.]com/macros/s/{id}/exec that answers with a 302 to script.googleusercontent.com carrying Base64+XOR(0xAC) task payloads. A new inter-component broker (rnp.dll, masquerading as the RNP OpenPGP library) routes messages between DLL modules and supports runtime upgrades. Coverage adds the DNS-channel-selection mechanism, the GAS relay request shape for egress detection, the leaked relay backend api.studiotikva[.]com/ac, and new file hashes and domain/IP indicators.

item.title: Clop-linked Windchill JSP web shell decrypts keystore credentials
item.description: Updated the PTC Windchill / FlexPLM CVE-2026-12569 page with ReliaQuest's August 19 reporting, corroborated by Ransom-ISAC with eCrime.ch and Defused, that a JSP web shell deployed after CVE-2026-12569 exploitation is a bespoke PLM-specific extortion platform attributed to the Clop (Cl0p) ransomware operation. The implant maps sensitive vault data, decrypts every credential in the Windchill keystore without additional tooling, and executes additional code via a custom Java class loader, converting the web shell into a backdoor for lateral movement, ransomware deployment, and persistence. Coverage records the attribution chain, the keystore-decryption and class-loader mechanics, and defender priorities including keystore access alerts and JSP web-shell hunting on Windchill / FlexPLM deployments.

item.title: SilkParasite: China-nexus Central Asia espionage cluster with five new RAT families
item.description: Added SilkParasite, a previously unreported cyber-espionage operation targeting Central Asian government bodies assessed by Bitdefender Labs as a medium-confidence China-nexus threat cluster discovered in late 2025. The operation deploys seven RAT families, five previously undocumented: DriveSilkRAT, CookiETagRAT, NomadRAT, GoginRAT, and NodeEdgeRAT, plus updated BLOODALCHEMY (a Deed/ShadowPad/PlugX-lineage backdoor first documented by Elastic in October 2023) and an updated SpiceRAT. Initial access uses password-protected RAR archives with malicious Office documents whose macros check for Kaspersky before executing a DLL-sideloading sequence; lures are tailored to ministries in Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Kazakhstan. Bitdefender characterizes the tooling as expert human-developed espionage code with traces of AI-assisted development, citing Go test functions, a hard-coded AES key set to 0123456789abcdef, and a change_this_key configuration field as the clearest artifacts.

item.title: Operation CameraSwarm: 14,500+ Dahua cameras compromised via auth bypass and P2P relay
item.description: Added Hunt.io's disclosure of Operation CameraSwarm, a campaign that compromised more than 14,530 Dahua cameras between June 17 and July 22, 2026 using credential attacks, two 2021 authentication-bypass flaws (CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045, both in CISA KEV), and a peer-to-peer relay technique. Confirmed compromises were concentrated in Ukraine and Russia. The campaign was reconstructed from a 407 MB exposed working directory containing 2,616 files across 234 subdirectories of tooling, logs, shell history, and campaign records, including Easy4IP serial-number P2P relay infrastructure first analyzed by ITRES Labs in October 2025. Coverage records the NetKeyboard loopback-login abuse, the serial-number relay mechanics, and defender priorities for Dahua deployments.

item.title: StopAndProtect: ~2,000 hacked WordPress sites powering distributed malware and ransomware
item.description: Added Check Point Research's tracking of StopAndProtect, a global cybercrime operation abusing close to 2,000 hacked WordPress websites as infrastructure to disseminate malware, commandeer infected hosts, and store stolen documents, screenshots, and activity logs. The operator's opsec blunders (exposed infection logs, victim screenshots, and mass-management tooling on the compromised sites) gave visibility into the campaign. The infection chain starts with ClickFix social engineering: a fake CAPTCHA overlay on a compromised WordPress site shown to non-Windows visitors via a malicious MU plugin instructs the visitor to copy-paste a command that deploys .NET downloaders and loaders, then a distributed toolkit that encrypts files, steals documents, locks screens via an SMB/USB-spreading VBS worm, and operates a live attacker-victim chat. Coverage records the infection chain, the malware family of the same name found in mid-May 2026, and the 6,000+ victim IP count Check Point's telemetry indicated as of July 24, 2026.

item.title: CoSnitch: Microsoft Copilot Personal one-click data exfiltration (CVE-2026-24301)
item.description: Added Varonis Threat Labs' disclosure of three vulnerabilities in Microsoft Copilot Personal collectively named CoSnitch, in which a single click on a crafted link silently pulls data from connected apps using the undocumented URL parameter autorun=1 (discovered via meta-hacking of the assistant itself). Varonis reported the issue in December 2025; Microsoft patched it on August 18, 2026 as CVE-2026-24301. The exfiltration request is indistinguishable at the network layer from ordinary Copilot web-page summarization fetches, the prompt runs to completion even if the victim closes the tab, and a separate memory-injection path writes an instruction that survives password changes, session revocation, and device re-enrollment with no endpoint-visible artifact. No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported; M365 Copilot is not stated to be affected.

item.title: MLflow CVE-2026-64849 SSRF: cloud-credential and secret exfiltration via model-registry webhooks
item.description: Added watchTowr and VulnCheck August 18 reporting that two open-source products are under active malicious scanning and exploitation: MLflow CVE-2026-64849, a flaw in model-registry webhooks that proxies requests through the affected system to reach cloud metadata services and exfiltrate cloud credentials and secrets, and FUXA CVE-2026-25895, a path traversal in the open-source web-based SCADA/HMI that observed attackers use to overwrite main.js with junk data (destructive DoS, no RCE observed in public reporting). watchTowr's global honeypot telemetry shows attackers indiscriminately scanning for exposed MLflow instances within hours of the CVE being assigned on August 17, 2026, targeting cloud-hosted MLflow systems to extract credentials from well-known internal IP addresses.

item.title: Gogs CVE-2026-52813 path-traversal RCE and remaining unpatched bypass
item.description: Added Aikido's report (via Aikido Attack AI pentesting) of flaws in Gogs, the open-source self-hosted Git platform, headlined by CVE-2026-52813 (GHSA-c39w-43gm-34h5), a path traversal to Remote Code Execution caused by UserPath() in repox.go joining the username with the repositories root directory without sanitizing ../ sequences. Gogs maintainers fixed the reported issues in 0.14.3, but one unpatched bypass of a reported vulnerability and the push-authorization bypass CVE-2026-52810 remain unfixed, plus GHSA-6vxv-wg6j-5qwp XSS via Jupyter notebookjs. Aikido recommends using a different self-hosted Git solution while Gogs is not actively maintained. No in-the-wild exploitation of CVE-2026-52813 has been reported.

item.title: TWINLOOT: modular Python implant running M365 C2 inside trusted Microsoft services
item.description: Added Ontinue Cyber Defense Center's disclosure of TWINLOOT, a previously undocumented PyArmor-hardened modular Python implant framework discovered during a July 2026 campaign investigation, whose defining characteristic is operating its entire C2 infrastructure inside trusted Microsoft services: tasking through SharePoint Online file dead-drops via the Microsoft Graph API, interactive operator access through WebRTC DataChannels relayed by Microsoft Teams TURN servers, and Graph-API traffic driven through a headless instance of the victim's own Edge browser over Chrome DevTools Protocol. Ontinue describes it as the first tool to combine M365 dead-drop C2, Teams TURN relay abuse, and headless-browser transport under one umbrella. Coverage records the infection and C2 architecture, pixel-perfect fake lock screens for Windows credential harvesting, reverse SOCKS5 pivots, and defender priorities including STAC4749 / Chaos overlap assessment when Teams vishing delivery pairs with a PyArmor Python backdoor.

item.title: AI "mind viruses": agent-to-agent spread via persistent prompt files
item.description: Added the Anthropic/EPFL August 10, 2026 preprint demonstrating that self-propagating payloads can spread between AI agents through the editable system-prompt files (SOUL.md, MEMORY.md) that autonomous agent harnesses persist across sessions, tested in a simulated six-agent coding collaboration and OpenClaw-modeled agent chains. In the observed propagation, agents writing payloads into SOUL.md accounted for 88% of attempts with 55% next-agent infection; ordinary workspace files accounted for 12% of attempts with 17% success. A one-paragraph warning in the system prompt reduced spread to near zero, and 15 generations of adversarial optimization against that warning (150+ payloads, Claude Haiku 4.5) produced no multi-hop strain. A review of Moltbook archives found no successful in-the-wild agent-to-agent propagation; the authors assess a real but currently limited risk. Defender priorities treat agent prompt/memory files as attack surface and add a one-paragraph anti-propagation warning plus cross-session persistence anomaly detection.

item.title: Apache Zeppelin CVE-2026-44613 CSRF into unauthorized notebook actions
item.description: Added OX Security's August 6 analysis of CVE-2026-44613, a cross-site request forgery in Apache Zeppelin 0.6.0 through 0.12.0 fixed in 0.12.1. The CorsFilter defaulted zeppelin.server.allowed.origins to *, accepting credentialed, state-changing cross-origin requests, and some endpoints accepted text/plain bodies that skip the CORS preflight entirely. A malicious page can therefore drive an authenticated Zeppelin session into forged administrative REST and WebSocket actions. Coverage records the CVSS 6.1 High vector, the 0.12.1 fix (empty default allow-list plus JSON-only content-type enforcement), the April-June-July disclosure-to-public timeline, and defender priorities including allow-list hardening and hunting for cross-origin administrative requests. No public exploitation or actor linkage has been reported; not in CISA KEV as of the last scan.

item.title: TheHatman: Microsoft Entra tenant credential-theft and forum sale claims
item.description: Added Unit 42's August 18 update to its Large-Scale Credential Attacks threat brief, which tracks an actor using the handle TheHatman who posted across multiple forums from August 1-17, 2026 offering to sell employee information for multiple enterprises. TheHatman allegedly exfiltrated data from organizations' Microsoft Entra tenants and claims access was gained through MFA fatigue and password spraying, but Unit 42 has not verified the claims or identified an intrusion vector, and the brief names no victims. Coverage records the claims-versus-evidence split, MFA fatigue and password-spray hunting pivots, the brief's recommendation to audit for successful logins shortly after large password-failure events, phishing-resistant MFA and Conditional Access hardening, and response steps if forum posts implicate your tenant.

item.title: Entra ID rogue device registration and AI-generated identifiers
item.description: Added Wiz Research's August 18 analysis of how AI-generated device names and User-Agent strings are eroding static Entra ID device-registration detection. The post measures nearly one in seven Entra ID environments hit by rogue DRS device registration in a 90-day window, notes the DESKTOP-XXXXXXXX pattern affects about one in ten customer environments, documents ROADrecon-era atomic IOCs (Dsreg/10.0 User-Agent, DESKTOP names, trivial microsoft-XXXXXXXX variants), the observed MSTokens-PRT/1.0. User-Agent registering a device named Work PC, the AWS 3.149.231.11 multi-victim device-code source and lockwall.xyz/prime/ shared-document phishing page, and pivots to behavioral detection: naming-convention anomaly baselining plus device-code-phishing-to-registration correlation, with MFA-for-device-registration as the hardening control and a tenant-naming-convention KQL baseline query.

item.title: macOS ClickFix campaign: MacSync Stealer behavioral pivots and rotating infrastructure
item.description: Updated the macOS ClickFix campaign page with Microsoft Defender Experts' August 18 MacSync Stealer follow-up. RST Cloud identified the threat through a limited domain set and documented rapid C2 replacement after public disclosure; Microsoft correlated recurring endpoints and network behaviors instead and connected more than 30 domains. Coverage records the /curl/, /dynamic?txd=, and /gate?buildtxd= request shapes, the custom api-key header, chunked HTTP PUT exfiltration with upload_id/chunk_index/total_chunks parameters, staged compressed archives, shared static api-key values across four C2 domains with per-deployment rotating build tokens, RST Cloud's eleven candidate-domain pivots, and chunked-exfiltration detection corollaries for hunting across rotating domains.

item.title: vm2 NodeVM host state exposure and DNS hijack (GHSA-m5w8-4gq2-6f8x)
item.description: Added OX Security's analysis of vm2 through 3.11.5, where the documented builtin: ['*'] wildcard admitted the os and dns Node built-ins into the sandbox, letting sandboxed code read the host process owner's identity, enumerate host interfaces, and call dns.setServers() to rewrite the host process-wide DNS resolver list with no notification to the embedder. Coverage records the CVSS 10.0 GHSA-m5w8-4gq2-6f8x advisory, the denylist-inversion root cause, the 3.11.6 fix that adds os and dns to DANGEROUS_BUILTINS at both enforcement layers, upgrade notes for code calling os.platform()/EOL/tmpdir(), the still-exposed child_process wildcard caveat, and DNS-resolver and identity-read detections.

item.title: GitLab GraphQL CVE-2026-19478 / CVE-2026-19650 critical patch
item.description: Added GitLab's August 17 critical patch release (19.2.4, 19.1.6, 19.0.8, 18.11.11) fixing two GraphQL vulnerabilities in self-managed CE/EE. CVE-2026-19478 (CVSS 9.4, CWE-94) lets an unauthenticated remote user modify or delete public projects through the rolling-deploy @gl_introduced version-filtering path by synthesizing a resolver-less field that dispatches to an attacker-chosen object method; CVE-2026-19650 (CVSS 7.1, CWE-352) lets multiplex-query document swapping execute GET mutations, breaking GitLab's read-only GET protection. Coverage records the NilResolver and per-tracer-hash patches, the four-branch affected range, the absence of a configuration workaround, unauthenticated-write compromise hunts, and the no-KEV/no-exploitation status as of the last scan.

item.title: npm bin-entry dependency confusion: Google-scoped bin name harvesting
item.description: Added SafeDep's writeup of an August 12 campaign that published 21 npm packages squatting CLI binary names exposed by Google's scoped packages through the bin field rather than package names, bypassing every standard dependency-confusion mitigation. Each package carried a minimal postinstall beacon posting a system fingerprint to a per-package C2 subdomain under *.instances.poc.jchunt[.]top; all 21 were unpublished within about an hour and recovered from npmmirror.com. Coverage records the 21 package names and versions, the publisher rootdaddy-msrc, the two-wave publish timeline, the source.txt breadcrumb methodology, the three unclaimed non-published names, the mitigation gap table, and a scope-wide bin-entry audit recipe.

item.title: CISA KEV August 17–18 additions: Microsoft IKE, Ray, VMware vCenter, SharePoint, macOS
item.description: Added CISA's August 17–18 KEV entries: Microsoft IKE Service Extensions CVE-2026-33824 (double free, RCE), VMware vCenter CVE-2026-59310 (Syslog path traversal, RCE), Microsoft SharePoint CVE-2026-55040 (weak authentication bypass), Apple macOS CVE-2026-65400 (Screen Sharing improper authentication), and Ray-Project CVE-2025-62593 (browser-exploitable code injection, GHSA-q279-jhrf-cc6v, fixed in 2.52.0). Coverage records the August 20/21 BOD 26-04 deadlines, exact fixed builds where available, the VMware vCenter escalation from "no evidence of exploitation" to confirmed known exploitation, and defender priorities that keep post-exploitation scoping separate from patching. CISA records ransomware use as unknown and does not link the five entries to a shared campaign.

item.title: Wiz Red Agent finds Snowflake GitHub Actions script injection leading to Jira credential exfiltration
item.description: Added Wiz Research's reporting of its autonomous Red Agent AI security-research tool identifying a critical GitHub Actions workflow script-injection in snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net. An unauthenticated issue title interpolated into a jira_issue.yml run block gave command execution on Snowflake's CI runner; GitHub Advanced Security scanned the vulnerable revision without flagging it. Coverage records the five-day exposure window, responsible disclosure and same-day patching, Jira token exfiltration and rotation, runner and IP pivots, and the August 17 clarification that Copilot co-author review checked the merged PR without catching the flaw.

item.title: CloudSEK publishes TeamPCP victim dataset: 78,330 secrets from 2,186 organizations; Wiz CIRT documents multi-org PAT mass-cloning campaign
item.description: Added StepSecurity's analysis of the CloudSEK TeamPCP exposure dataset (78,330 distinct secrets from 2,186 organizations, March 19-24, 2026, with GitLab the most affected platform and 157 leaked OpenAI API keys) and Wiz CIRT's coordinated multi-organization GitHub PAT campaign (readme reconnaissance from 13.221.167.217, validation clones from 107.174.201.183, and 102 ca-central-1 AWS IPs mass-cloning up to thousands of repositories per organization on June 1). Coverage records secret-class breakdowns, investigation playbooks, audit-log retention limits, and the unconfirmed initial access vector.

item.title: Baileys / libsignal-node npm campaign: silent WhatsApp channel-follow abuse
item.description: Added SafeDep's August 10, 2026 analysis of a campaign of npm packages that fork Baileys, the WhatsApp Web multi-device library, and use the installer's already-paired session to force the installer's own WhatsApp account to follow attacker-controlled channels — non-consensual social abuse shipped through npm, not credential theft. The confirmed lower-bound set is 70 Baileys-based names across 343 versions plus 15 libsignal-node impersonators across 38 versions (4,250 "baileys" and 112 "libsignal-node" names exist in the registry, most unexamined). Coverage records the five distinct abuse mechanics — hard-coded channel follow on connection.open (@neykoor), remote-controlled follow-plus-mute list from raw.githubusercontent.com (lupy4u), character-code-obfuscated advertising URL injected into outgoing media previews (mamz-baileys), forged forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo channel attribution with noSelfSync on outgoing messages (@cikikomo), and a base64 gintoki authorisation gate that sends "you are no longer authorized" from the victim's account and blocks the bot (@prototypevip) — along with publisher list, newsletter JIDs, levvleys.json and levvicode[.]cloud operator infrastructure, source-verification status per package, and defender priorities (pin upstream baileys/libsignal-node, audit newsletter.js / messages-send.js / luxu.js / prototype-store.js, alert on bot-runtime fetches of untrusted repos, review muted channel follows on affected accounts, and revoke paired sessions).

item.title: Coding-agent hooks as audit telemetry: logging every AI coding-agent tool call
item.description: Added Elastic Security Labs' August 11, 2026 write-up of an internal program that gives developers an AI coding agent (Cursor) with shell, file, and MCP access and records everything the agent does: a 280-line dependency-free bash script fired by Cursor lifecycle hooks writes every tool call as JSONL, and the Elastic Agent filestream ships it to Elasticsearch. Since the May 2026 rollout, over 13 million tool-call events from 1,100+ machines and nearly 900 distinct users have been logged, with file reads dominating shell execution roughly 4:1. Coverage records the durable defender pattern — a coding agent with shell access is indistinguishable from the developer in EDR, and lifecycle hooks (sessionStart, before/afterShellExecution, before/afterMCPExecution, postToolUse, afterFileEdit, subagentStart, stop) close that gap as a sensor that approves everything and records everything — plus the full hook-to-event mapping, deployment gotchas (space-free script path, hooks.json read only at startup, passwd-based home resolution), the filestream/decode_json_fields integration, ES|QL examples, and the DNS-logs-style privacy treatment (ai_hooks.* namespace excluded from general-purpose security roles via field-level security). The article is a defensive-telemetry pattern, not an attribution report; the blocking-hook capability and read-heavy/CLI-undercounted fleet statistics are noted with their limits.

item.title: Kimwolf v7 hardens Android/IoT DDoS operations with HTTP/2 fingerprints, ENS, and Tor
item.description: Added Unit 42's analysis of Kimwolf v7, an Android TV and set-top-box DDoS bot in the AISURU operator ecosystem. Coverage records residential-proxy access to unauthenticated ADB, externalized propagation, 15 flood methods, Chrome-like HTTP/2 fingerprints, ENS resolution through public Ethereum RPC, a moderate-confidence operator RPC facade, Tor and localhost-proxy fallback, hashes, historical infrastructure, and response guidance.

item.title: Grafana MCP turns a caller-selected destination into a readable SSRF proxy
item.description: Added Grafana's critical CVE-2026-19516 advisory. Grafana MCP Server and mcp-grafana through 1.0.0 accepted a caller-selected X-Grafana-URL while grafana_api_request exposed method, path, and body controls, enabling readable SSRF to internal, loopback, link-local, and metadata services. Coverage records why the earlier credential-binding fix was incomplete, the 1.1.0 header removal and optional caller authentication, exposure hunts, and the absence of reported exploitation.

item.title: LangGraph namespace prefix matching crosses tenant boundaries
item.description: Added CVE-2026-71433 / GHSA-47pj-3jcm-6whg to the LangGraph checkpointer trust-boundary analysis. PostgreSQL and SQLite stores used non-segment-aware namespace pattern matching, allowing ordinary scoped reads to return sibling tenant data for prefix-colliding, wildcard-bearing, suffix-matching, or case-colliding labels. Coverage records affected hosted deployments, the 3.1.1 fixes, audit pivots, and the absence of reported exploitation.

item.title: Aeternum turns Polygon smart contracts into a durable botnet control plane
item.description: Added Unit 42's analysis of Aeternum's C++, PyInstaller, and Python malware branches. Coverage records the shared Polygon getDomain selector and operator update path, weakly encrypted and plaintext on-chain instructions, Windows Startup and Early Bird APC persistence, GitHub, Pastebin, Telegram, and HTTP dependencies, XWorm and XMRig payloads, wallet-focused collection, durable hashes and infrastructure pivots, detection guidance, and attribution limits.

item.title: Gunra affiliates turn Fortinet and VDI access into cross-platform double extortion
item.description: Added the joint CISA, FBI, DC3, NSA, U.S. Secret Service, and KNPA advisory on Gunra ransomware-as-a-service. Coverage records observed FortiOS and FortiProxy exploitation, VPN and VDI session abuse, an attacker-selected OTP bypass, Impacket lateral movement, OneDrive and SharePoint exfiltration reaching tens of terabytes in one case, primary and disaster-recovery backup deletion, encryption artifacts, historical indicators, and response priorities.

item.title: DeadLock ransomware decentralizes recovery chat and leak infrastructure
item.description: Added Microsoft Threat Intelligence's technical analysis of the Rust-based DeadLock double-extortion operation. Coverage records more than 80 leak-site claims, resource-aware and intermittent XChaCha20 encryption, backup and logging impairment, Polygon smart-contract configuration, Session encrypted chat, Wasabi leak storage, durable host and network pivots, and the remaining off-chain dependencies in its decentralized recovery stack.

item.title: Six npm packages use the NullReceiver Ethereum dead-drop loader
item.description: Added Sonatype's same-day report on three hijacked legitimate npm packages and three newly published packages carrying one JavaScript loader. Coverage records exact versions, redundant Ethereum RPC and Blockscout resolution, /0x/cls and /0x/ls staging, X-Payload-B64 HEAD-response fallback, in-process and detached execution, response guidance, and the source-linked but carefully bounded Contagious Interview and PolinRider relationships.

item.title: Flyto2 sends its internal runner secret to a caller-selected callback
item.description: Added GitHub's reviewed Flyto2 Core CVE-2026-67426 / GHSA-jx74-cqjv-2c67. The unauthenticated flyto-verification /run service accepted a caller-selected callback URL, made an outbound request, and attached the internal runner secret; coverage records the SSRF and callback-forgery impact, 2.26.7 fix, secret rotation and egress hunts, and the absence of reported exploitation.

item.title: Metabase zero-day root cause and downstream customer-data impact
item.description: Added Wiz Research's reverse engineering of GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf, including the request-merge and HoneySQL raw-SQL path, public proof-of-concept status, and cloud exposure measurements. First-party n8n and Anaconda/Kilo Code notices now confirm downstream access to customer records, a small number of password hashes and Slack tokens, and possible AI prompt exposure.

item.title: OpenAI pauses insufficiently isolated Astra work after it cannot rule out a critical cyber threshold
item.description: Added OpenAI's disclosure that preliminary Astra evaluations were strong enough that it could not rule out its Critical cyber-capability threshold.
