item.title: Klue Salesforce OAuth token abuse
item.description: Added coverage for the Klue integration incident affecting connected customer SaaS environments: a compromised legacy integration credential reportedly let an attacker obtain OAuth tokens, query customer CRM data including Salesforce, and trigger Salesforce to disable the Klue Battlecards app integration. The page captures Klue, Huntress, Salesforce, and The Hacker News reporting, plus SaaS OAuth grant triage, connected-app logging, token revocation, and stale vendor-credential controls.

item.title: npm install explicit-trust controls: developer package-config drift update
item.description: Updated the npm install explicit-trust controls pattern with StepSecurity's developer-machine package-configuration guidance: internal registries, secure registries, package cooldowns, and auth policy only protect hosts actually configured to use them. The page now captures npm and Python package-manager config inventory, public-index fallback detection, endpoint cooldown enforcement, token hygiene, and drift monitoring across developer laptops and CI runners.

item.title: Agent localhost control-plane RCE
item.description: Added a pattern page for Microsoft Security Research's AutoJack case study: untrusted web content rendered by a browsing AI agent can cross the localhost boundary, reach a local MCP WebSocket control plane, and turn caller-supplied stdio server parameters into host command execution. The page captures the AutoGen Studio development-branch caveat, upstream hardening before PyPI release, and durable guidance for authenticating loopback control planes, allowlisting MCP launchers, isolating browsing agents, and hunting agent-spawned child processes.

item.title: GHOST STADIUM FIFA World Cup ticket phishing
item.description: Added coverage for Hunt.io's June 17 GHOST STADIUM FIFA World Cup 2026 ticketing phishing report: cloned FIFA ticketing portals on lookalike domains, same-origin credential and payment harvesting, reusable /fifa/ React-build and Layui pivots, suspected AS25820 / 16clouds origin hosting, favicon clustering, and a caveated Chinese-speaking operator assessment.

item.title: procwire / routecraft npm Windows dropper
item.description: Added coverage for SafeDep's June 18 report on a five-package npm campaign: procwire and routecraft execute a Windows-only preinstall dropper while bytecraft, endpointmap, and staticlayer split XOR endpoint reconstruction and payload-serving logic across helper packages. The page captures package/version pivots, files.catbox.moe staging, Microsoft-Delivery-Optimization User-Agent gating, updater-like temp executable names, Mark-of-the-Web stripping, and Windows npm-install response guidance.

item.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 KEV exploitation update
item.description: Updated the Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 page after CISA added the unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service flaw to KEV on 2026-06-18. The update records known exploitation, the 2026-07-09 federal remediation due date, emergency isolation or upgrade guidance for internet-facing Splunk Web / management surfaces, and the existing watchTowr backup / restore endpoint hunting pivots.

item.title: AI scanner anti-analysis
item.description: Added a pattern page for Socket's shai_hulululud npm package analysis: source-code comments, safety-triggering text, context flooding, and staged obfuscation can make AI-assisted package scanners refuse, truncate, time out, misclassify, or fail open before reaching executable code. The page captures scanner-hardening guidance for untrusted source text, executable-code prioritization, context-flood detection, deterministic preprocessing, and fail-closed handling.

item.title: Vertex AI staging-bucket squatting
item.description: Added a pattern page for Unit 42's Pickle in the Middle Vertex AI SDK research: deterministic default staging-bucket names plus missing ownership checks in google-cloud-aiplatform 1.139.0 and 1.140.0 let attackers squat expected buckets, race-replace uploaded joblib / pickle model artifacts, and trigger code execution in Vertex AI serving infrastructure. The page captures upgrade guidance for 1.148.0+, explicit staging_bucket controls, bucket-ownership hunts, and model-artifact provenance checks.

item.title: Mastra easy-day-js npm scope compromise: Microsoft follow-up
item.description: Updated the Mastra easy-day-js npm scope compromise page with Microsoft Threat Intelligence's June 17 follow-up: exact observed publish times, 4,572-byte setup.cjs dropper details, XOR-encoded .pkg_logs marker behavior, legacy IE8 User-Agent ICAP-style exfiltration, Windows reflective .NET loading and cmd.exe injection, and additional setup.cjs / easy-day-js tarball hashes.

item.title: Mastra easy-day-js npm scope compromise: SafeDep follow-up
item.description: Updated the Mastra easy-day-js npm scope compromise page with SafeDep's June 17 follow-up: provenance dropped on attacker-published packages, the 01:12-02:36 UTC scope-wide republish burst, sergey2016 and ehindero2016 email-pattern overlap, User-Agent-gated stage-two retrieval, Hostwinds raw-IP infrastructure, wolfSSL test-certificate pivot, second-stage SHA-256, and a caveated BlueNoroff / Sapphire Sleet tradecraft overlap note.

item.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-54420 exploitation
item.description: Added coverage for active exploitation of LiteSpeed's user-end cPanel plugin CVE-2026-54420: FTP or web-shell access on CloudLinux / CageFS shared-hosting systems can escalate to root before cPanel plugin 2.4.8 / WHM Plugin 5.3.2.1. The page captures CISA KEV status, LiteSpeed's generateEcCert and packageUserSize log pivots, concurrency and same-source-IP triage clues, plugin removal fallback, and root-compromise response guidance.

item.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20262 arbitrary file write update
item.description: Updated the Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager exploitation page with CVE-2026-20262, Cisco's June 15 authenticated web-UI arbitrary-file-write advisory. The update captures CISA KEV status, the valid-write-access precondition, root-escalation risk through crafted file upload, suspicious WAR deployment paths under WildFly, /var/log/nms log pivots, and how this companion issue changes SD-WAN Manager control-plane triage alongside CVE-2026-20245.

item.title: Joomla JCE CVE-2026-48907 exploitation
item.description: Added coverage for CISA KEV CVE-2026-48907 in Widget Factory's JCE / Joomla Content Editor extension: unauthenticated profile import can create rogue editor profiles that permit PHP uploads and execution. The page captures Widget Factory's active-exploitation warning, public exploit-code caveat, profiles.import log pivot, suspicious JCE profile and PHP-upload artifacts, JCE 2.9.99.6 guidance, and cleanup sequencing for already-compromised Joomla sites.

item.title: Glassworm / GlassWASM Open VSX extension wave
item.description: Updated the Glassworm developer supply-chain botnet page with Socket's GlassWASM reporting: trojanized Open VSX copies of exargd/vsblack and noellee-doc/flint-debug used TinyGo WebAssembly, encrypted runtime strings, Solana SPL Memo dead-drop tasking, and OS-specific download-and-execute templates. The update adds extension, wallet, memo-program, hash, and editor-directory hunting pivots while keeping the VS Code Marketplace originals scoped as clean.

item.title: Crypto Clipper Tor / USB worm
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported a Windows cryptocurrency clipper campaign active since February 2026. The new page captures malicious LNK and USB propagation, Defender exclusions, scheduled-task persistence, WScript / ActiveX execution, Task Manager anti-analysis checks, bundled Tor client ugate.exe, localhost:9050 hidden-service C2, clipboard seed/private-key theft, wallet-address substitution, screenshot exfiltration, EVAL tasking, and behavior-first hunting guidance.

item.title: Mastra easy-day-js npm scope compromise
item.description: Added coverage for the June 17, 2026 Mastra npm scope compromise reported by StepSecurity, Socket, and Snyk: a stale npm maintainer account republished more than 140 @mastra packages with a transitive easy-day-js dependency, whose postinstall loader fetched a cross-platform Node.js implant with Windows, macOS, and Linux persistence. The page captures affected-scope caveats, stale-access root cause, loader and C2 pivots, and host/CI response guidance.

item.title: Crypto supply-chain path to transaction authority
item.description: Added a pattern page from Sygnia's crypto supply-chain analysis: developer endpoint and identity compromise can flow through repositories, CI/CD workflows, automation identities, cloud and Kubernetes control planes, secrets stores, vendor channels, custody APIs, wallet orchestration, and transaction authority. The page captures containment-first controls for workflow changes, service-account keys, Kubernetes exec, vendor API abuse, and custody/signing correlation.

item.title: Mr_Rot13 cPanel CVE-2026-41940 backdoor campaign: watchTowr session-forgery analysis
item.description: Updated the Mr_Rot13 cPanel CVE-2026-41940 page with cPanel's fixed branch list and watchTowr's root-cause analysis: pre-auth whostmgrsession creation, stripped cookie ob suffixes, HTTP Basic CRLF injection into /var/cpanel/sessions/raw session files, forged hasroot / tfa_verified / cp_security_token fields, token-denied promotion into JSON session cache, and defender hunts for anomalous cPanel session artifacts and WHM API access after failed logins.

item.title: Outsider Enterprise smishing PhaaS
item.description: Google reported and filed civil litigation against Outsider Enterprise, a China-based, Telegram-coordinated SMS phishing-kit network. The new page captures Google's reporting on Gemini-assisted phishing-page generation, 9,000 fake websites, more than 1 million fraudulent URLs, 55,000 Android-user spam reports, 2.5 million Android-user messages in two weeks, brokerage-account and mobile-carrier reward lures, and Google / FBI / carrier disruption paths.

item.title: Operation DangerousPassword axios npm compromise: Hunt.io payload analysis
item.description: Updated the Operation DangerousPassword / axios npm compromise page with Hunt.io's reverse-engineering of the plain-crypto-js payload chain: clean-to-weaponized package staging, reversed-Base64 plus XOR obfuscation, macOS Mach-O / Windows PowerShell / Linux Python RAT delivery, sfrclak[.]com:8000 product0/product1/product2 routing, shared RAT commands, Windows MicrosoftUpdate Run-key persistence, macOS ad-hoc signing, and Hunt.io's TA444 / BlueNoroff infrastructure assessment.

item.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 pre-auth file write / RCE
item.description: Splunk disclosed CVE-2026-20253, a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated arbitrary file creation and truncation issue in the Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Service endpoint. watchTowr Labs showed how Splunk Web proxy access to /splunkd/__raw/v1/postgres/recovery/backup and restore paths can turn the file-write primitive into code execution by overwriting Splunk-executed Python scripts. The new page captures affected versions, Splunk Cloud non-exposure caveats, detection pivots, and patch guidance for Splunk Enterprise 10.2.4 / 10.0.7 or later.

item.title: Operation Highland Velvet Ant authentication-stack backdoors
item.description: Sygnia reported Operation Highland, a Velvet Ant intrusion with forensic artifacts dating back to 2016 in an internal network with no direct internet connectivity. The new page captures the China-nexus actor's staged access through internet-facing systems, GS-Netcat and SOCKS5 tunneling, Nginx / FastCGI execution paths, backdoored pam_unix.so and OpenSSH binaries, credential capture, SSH keylogging, authorized_keys persistence, and responder guidance for verifying and replacing compromised authentication components before credential rotation.

item.title: Velvet Ant
item.description: New actor profile for Sygnia's Velvet Ant reporting, connecting Operation Highland authentication-stack backdoors with Sygnia's prior public reporting on F5 BIG-IP abuse, Cisco Nexus CVE-2024-20399 exploitation, and VELVETSHELL. The profile keeps attribution scoped to primary Sygnia sourcing and highlights the recurring defender lesson: include appliances, bastions, Linux authentication stacks, and management-plane systems in threat hunts.

item.title: Chrome live-wallpaper extension ad-fraud network
item.description: Socket Security Research reported a Chrome Web Store operation using 152 new-tab live-wallpaper extensions across 38 publisher accounts and three brand backends. The new page captures the tabplugins Google organic-attribution forgery, cloaked uninstall redirects, false privacy disclosures, IndexedDB anti-forensic fingerprint, publisher-fragmentation evasion, and defender guidance for extension allow-listing and enterprise browser hunting.

item.title: Atomic Arch AUR package hijack
item.description: Sonatype Security Research and StepSecurity reported Atomic Arch, a June 2026 AUR supply-chain campaign where attackers adopted orphaned Arch User Repository packages and changed PKGBUILD / install logic to fetch malicious npm dependencies such as atomic-lockfile, js-digest, and lockfile-js. The new page captures the orphan-package trust-inheritance path, cross-ecosystem npm / Bun fetch behavior, native Linux credential-stealer payload, Arch / WSL2 / self-hosted-runner exposure, and defender guidance for package-script review, endpoint triage, and credential rotation.

item.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 exploitation: Arctic Wolf follow-up
item.description: Arctic Wolf reported CVE-2026-0257 intrusions where cookie-based GlobalProtect authentication led to unauthorized IPsec VPN tunnel establishment and rapid SMB / NTLM reconnaissance consistent with Impacket tooling. The updated page adds exposure preconditions, authentication and tunnel event sequences, VPS / Tor / unusual-geography pivots, suspicious device names such as GP-CLIENT / DESKTOP-GP01 / kali, and responder guidance for mapping gateway-connected events to internal activity from VPN-assigned addresses.

item.title: Astro config blockchain C2 PR injection
item.description: SafeDep reported a malicious pull request that hid an obfuscated blockchain-C2 loader inside homepage/astro.config.mjs while posing as a benign dashboard fix. The page captures Astro config execution risk, horizontal-whitespace diff hiding, Tron-to-Binance Smart Chain second-stage resolution, SafeDep's PolinRider attribution caveat, and defender guidance for pull-request review, developer endpoint triage, and CI credential rotation.

item.title: Void Dokkaebi
item.description: Trend Micro reports that Void Dokkaebi, also tracked as Famous Chollima, has migrated InvisibleFerret from readable Python scripts to Cython-compiled Python extension modules distributed as .pyd files on Windows and .so files on macOS. The new profile captures BeaverTail evolution, fake recruiter / developer-targeting tradecraft, Cython launcher-script detection gaps, browser credential theft, wallet-extension trojanization, macOS Chrome downgrade behavior, and defender guidance for binary-aware developer endpoint triage.

item.title: Sentry MCP Agentjacking
item.description: Tenet Security documented Agentjacking, an AI-agent trust-boundary pattern where attacker-injected Sentry error events can be relayed through the Sentry MCP server as trusted troubleshooting context. The page captures the public-DSN ingest path, markdown fake-remediation injection, npx/package-manager execution risk in Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex workflows, and defender guidance for treating observability records as untrusted input before agent tool execution.

item.title: LangGraph checkpointer injection and unsafe deserialization
item.description: Check Point Research disclosed a LangGraph checkpointer vulnerability chain affecting self-hosted AI-agent services that expose checkpoint-history filtering with user-controlled keys. The page captures CVE-2025-67644 SQLite filter-key SQL injection, CVE-2026-28277 unsafe msgpack checkpoint deserialization, CVE-2026-27022 Redis / RediSearch query injection, the get_state_history() trust boundary, and defender guidance for patching, filter allow-listing, checkpoint-store review, and least-privilege agent runtimes.

item.title: Solana FakeFix npm / PyPI developer stealer
item.description: JFrog Security Research reports Solana FakeFix, a June 2026 malicious npm and PyPI package campaign aimed at Solana developers with patched-SDK lures, GitHub issue spam, npm postinstall execution, PyPI import-time payloads, Telegram C2, wallet-draining behavior, fake MEV private-key prompts, and CMS-themed Windows Deno loader persistence. The page captures affected package names, targeted secret paths, Solana wallet and RPC pivots, and defender guidance for developer workstations and CI runners.

item.title: Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 ShinyHunters exploitation
item.description: Google Mandiant and GTIG attribute active Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 zero-day exploitation to UNC6240 / ShinyHunters between 2026-05-27 and 2026-06-09. The page captures PSEMHUB and PSIGW endpoint exposure, higher-education targeting concentration, MeshCentral staging, fanout extortion scripts, ShinyHunters DLS linkage, and defender guidance for endpoint restriction, WebLogic log review, PSEMHUB filesystem inspection, and outbound SMB monitoring.

item.title: ShinyHunters
item.description: Narrow actor stub for Google Mandiant / GTIG's UNC6240 / ShinyHunters attribution in the June 2026 Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 campaign, capturing the extortion-driven PeopleSoft zero-day activity while keeping broader ShinyHunters ecosystem claims out until supported by primary reporting.

item.title: Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 exploitation
item.description: CISA added Ivanti Sentry CVE-2026-10520 to KEV on 2026-06-11 after public reporting identified a critical OS command-injection path that can allow unauthenticated root-level RCE on exposed, unmanaged Sentry appliances. The page captures fixed versions R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1, companion CVE-2026-10523 authentication bypass risk, watchTowr route analysis for /mics/api/v2/sentry/mics-config/handleMessage, and responder guidance for edge-appliance containment and log review.

item.title: GitHub Actions OIDC subject-claim collisions
item.description: Boost Security Labs disclosed a short-lived GitHub Actions OIDC immutable-subject preview issue where a hyphen delimiter allowed exact string collisions between victim immutable claims and attacker-controlled legacy namespaces. The page captures the Sleeper Squats pre-registration pattern, affected trust boundaries such as cloud IAM and trusted publishing, GitHub's current @ delimiter fix, and defender guidance to avoid broad string-only OIDC trust policies.

item.title: OceanLotus
item.description: ESET reports 2024-2026 OceanLotus / APT32 activity showing increased domestic Vietnamese espionage, including a selective FireAnt MetaKit stock-investor supply-chain compromise and a long-running Vietnamese infrastructure / transport construction intrusion. The new profile captures SPECTRALVIPER side-loading, encrypted Cookie-header beacons, named-pipe orchestration, FireAnt update-protocol weaknesses, and defender pivots for the reported campaigns.

item.title: JDY SOHO / IoT reconnaissance botnet
item.description: Lumen Black Lotus Labs reports JDY, a China-nexus reconnaissance botnet that grew from the earlier KV-botnet JDY cluster into more than 1,500 compromised SOHO and IoT devices. The page captures JDY's Tor-managed C2 and payload architecture, distributed service fingerprinting, rapid post-disclosure Fortinet scanning, MIPS-family Linux scanner behavior, Dispatch Service paths, and defender heuristics for residential-IP reconnaissance that can precede edge-device exploitation.

item.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 exploitation pivots
item.description: Unit 42 reports active exploitation of PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 by an unidentified actor attempting unauthorized VPN access. The updated page adds Unit 42's pre-PoC source IP pivots, suspicious generic host-ID and device-name values, the gateway-connected event triage focus, and Palo Alto Networks mitigation guidance for fixed releases, dedicated authentication-override certificates, or disabling authentication override.

item.title: SHADOW-AETHER AI-augmented Latin America intrusions
item.description: Trend Micro reports SHADOW-AETHER-040 and SHADOW-AETHER-064, likely distinct Latin America intrusion campaigns using agentic AI during operations against government and financial-sector targets. The page captures tunnel-first AI-assisted workflows through ProxyChains / SSH / Chisel / web shells, dynamic script generation, credential and configuration mining, custom backdoors such as implante_http, SHADOW-AETHER-064 POW / SOCKTZ tunneling tools, and defender guidance for detecting agentic post-exploitation inside victim networks.

item.title: ServiceNow instance unauthenticated table-query exploitation
item.description: ServiceNow disclosed a hosted-instance security issue after detecting anomalous activity and evidence of successful instance-table queries against a subset of customers. The page captures the unauthenticated access primitive, affected Australia-release / pre-Australia configuration caveat, hosted update on 2026-06-05, no-CVE / no-attribution caveat, and defender guidance for SaaS table, integration, and downstream-secret review.

item.title: Cloud logging control-plane tampering
item.description: Unit 42 describes cloud logging control-plane abuse against AWS CloudTrail and Google Cloud Logging: attackers with logging permissions can stop or delete log routes, delete destinations, impair decryption, poison mutable log objects, or redirect logs to attacker-controlled destinations for continuous visibility. The page captures defender heuristics for treating logging configuration as tier-zero, alerting on routing and destination changes, preserving immutable fallbacks, and validating log integrity during incident response.

item.title: Arista EOS CVE-2026-7473 tunnel decapsulation exploitation
item.description: CISA added Arista EOS CVE-2026-7473 to KEV on 2026-06-09 after Arista reported in-the-wild exploitation. The page captures the tunnel-decapsulation flaw affecting EOS devices configured as VXLAN, GRE, IP-in-IP, NVGRE, or GUE tunnel endpoints, the lack of a software-upgrade path, and defender guidance for endpoint inventory, ACL hardening, TCAM-change caution, and network-path review.

item.title: Chrome V8 CVE-2026-11645 exploitation
item.description: Google released Chrome Stable 149.0.7827.102/.103 for Windows and macOS and 149.0.7827.102 for Linux on 2026-06-08, and stated that an exploit for CVE-2026-11645 exists in the wild. The page captures the V8 out-of-bounds memory-access flaw, active-exploitation caveat, fixed builds, Chromium-derived browser follow-up, and defender response guidance for browser zero-day patching and endpoint review.

item.title: UAC-0226 / SHADOW-EARTH-066
item.description: Trend Micro reports that UAC-0226, temporarily tracked by Trend Micro as SHADOW-EARTH-066, shifted from macro-enabled Excel droppers to WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 exploit chains by February 2026. The profile captures GIFTEDCROOK evolution from plaintext Telegram browser-credential theft into an in-memory DLL chain with RC4-encrypted dedicated C2, Startup LNK execution, and browser/document theft against Ukrainian military, law-enforcement, and local-government targets.

item.title: Trend Micro WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 follow-up on Gamaredon and UAC-0226
item.description: Trend Micro reports that Earth Dahu / Gamaredon and UAC-0226 / SHADOW-EARTH-066 continued producing WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 exploit samples months after the July 2025 WinRAR 7.13 patch. The update separates Gamaredon's HTA / VBScript / Cloudflare Workers espionage flow from UAC-0226's Startup LNK, PowerShell, and evolved GIFTEDCROOK DLL chain, and highlights unmanaged WinRAR installations as a durable patch-management blind spot.

item.title: AI-brand impersonation phishing and malvertising
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports 2026 campaigns abusing AI brands such as ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, and Copilot as social-engineering lures for payment-card theft, AiTM credential/token theft, and Vidar/Lumma/Oyster/Hijack Loader malware delivery. The page captures the ChatGPT billing phish, Claude account-appeal PDF chain, Storm-3075 AI-plugin malvertising with Fox Tempest-signed payloads, fake DeepSeek V4 GitHub release assets, and defender heuristics for mail, identity, web, endpoint, and code-hosting surfaces.

item.title: Linux nftables CVE-2026-23111 public LPE exploits
item.description: Exodus Intelligence and FuzzingLabs have published working exploit research for CVE-2026-23111, a Linux kernel nf_tables use-after-free that can let an unprivileged local user escalate to root when nftables and user namespaces are reachable. The page captures the Debian, Ubuntu, and Red Hat reproduction context, no-remote-vector caveat, kernel patch / reboot guidance, and hardening priorities for container hosts, CI runners, and shared Linux systems.

item.title: Microsoft Teams external-chat phishing
item.description: Unit 42 reports that collaboration-tool phishing alerts represented 42% of phishing alerts in Cortex in the first four months of 2026, up from 30% in the prior four months. The page captures Microsoft Teams external-chat abuse through open federation, unmanaged accounts, typosquatted tenants, and compromised partner accounts, with defender guidance for Teams federation allow-listing, unmanaged-account restrictions, identity correlation, user reporting, and chat removal.

item.title: Quest KACE SMA CVE-2025-32975 exploitation
item.description: Hunt.io reports an exposed attacker toolkit and victim data tied to exploitation of Quest KACE Systems Management Appliance CVE-2025-32975, a critical SSO authentication-bypass flaw that can allow administrative takeover of a privileged endpoint-management appliance. The page captures the MSP/downstream-customer blast radius, 219-file / 308 MB exposed toolkit, reverse shells, account creation, SMB credential spraying, WMI reconnaissance, Earthworm / SOCKS5 tunneling, Tor staging, Quest fixed builds, and responder guidance for KACE appliance review.

item.title: Check Point VPN CVE-2026-50751 exploitation
item.description: Check Point Research reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-50751, a critical authentication-bypass flaw affecting Remote Access VPN and Mobile Access deployments configured to use deprecated IKEv1. The page captures the password-bypass VPN session primitive, 2026-05-07 earliest observed exploitation date, early-June increase, related CVE-2026-50752 IKEv1 certificate-validation issue, medium-confidence financially motivated / Qilin ransomware-affiliate assessment, and responder guidance for VPN logs, internal activity from VPN pools, hotfixing, and configuration mitigation.

item.title: UNK_DeadDrop developer repository phishing
item.description: Proofpoint reports UNK_DeadDrop, a likely North Korea-aligned developer-targeting phishing cluster that used recruitment, code-review, Foundry testing, and AI-payment lures to send targets to malicious GitHub and GitLab repositories. The page captures the VS Code / Cursor folderOpen task execution path, malicious VSIX persistence, Overlord payloads, cryptocurrency-wallet and browser credential theft, and Proofpoint's caveat that the cluster remains distinct from Contagious Interview in its telemetry.

item.title: VerdantBamboo appliance BRICKSTORM operation
item.description: Volexity reports a VerdantBamboo / WARP PANDA / UNC5221 appliance operation involving BRICKSTORM implants on Egnyte Storage Sync and pfSense systems, PLENET / GRIMBOLT on Synology NAS, AGENTPSD fallback persistence, likely MSP-enabled access, VPN and firewall re-entry, and long-running activity on low-EDR Linux and FreeBSD appliances. The page also captures Mandiant vSphere BRICKSTORM control-plane hardening lessons.

item.title: VerdantBamboo
item.description: VerdantBamboo is Volexity's name for a China-nexus espionage actor mapped to WARP PANDA and UNC5221. The profile captures appliance-first tradecraft against Egnyte Storage Sync, pfSense, Synology NAS, MSP, Linux, FreeBSD, and VMware-adjacent management-plane systems, with BRICKSTORM, PLENET / GRIMBOLT, and AGENTPSD malware coverage.

item.title: Hades graph-ML PyPI import-hook wave in the Miasma / Mini Shai-Hulud campaign
item.description: StepSecurity reports a June 8 Hades PyPI wave affecting graph machine-learning, computational-biology, bioinformatics, and genotype-phenotype packages. The update adds import-hook execution through package __init__.py, Bun v1.3.14 staging, LLM-analysis prompt-injection evasion, macOS and Windows runner-memory scrapers, GitHub-backed C2 keywords, SSH/SCP lateral movement, workflow-injection secret theft, and gh-token-monitor wiper-deterrent persistence.

item.title: Hades PyPI wheel wave in the Miasma / Mini Shai-Hulud campaign
item.description: Socket reports a PyPI branch of the Mini Shai-Hulud / Miasma lineage using Hades-themed markers: 37 malicious wheels across 19 packages, executable *-setup.pth Python-startup hooks, Bun v1.3.13 staging, obfuscated _index.js credential theft, GitHub exfiltration markers, and Hades-specific hashes and detection pivots.

item.title: Hunt.io global smishing infrastructure campaign
item.description: Hunt.io reports a coordinated smishing operation spanning 19 countries and 1,628 active malicious URLs impersonating government payment portals, road-police and tax services, parcel brands, telecoms, toll systems, banking / fine-payment portals, and retail rewards. The page captures the reusable 128-character HTML metadata hash, repeated JavaScript assets, URL-language pattern, target scope, hosting footprint, and defender pivots for brand-protection and web-telemetry teams.

item.title: Oman government Iranian-nexus webshell C2
item.description: Hunt.io reports an exposed RouterHosting VPS that revealed an Iranian-nexus intrusion campaign against Omani government entities, centered on the Ministry of Justice and Legal Affairs. The page captures the ASP.NET / DotNetNuke web shell path, Python and PowerShell C2 workflow, Chisel tunneling, SQL and identity-data collection, registry-hive theft, and Hunt.io's caveat that the activity sits in the broader Iranian state-nexus space without a group-level attribution.

item.title: MiniPlasma Windows Cloud Filter LPE exploitation
item.description: Kaspersky reports MiniPlasma, a public Windows Cloud Filter / CVE-2020-17103-adjacent local privilege-escalation exploit that can grant SYSTEM on fully updated Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025 systems before Microsoft's planned June 2026 patch. The page captures the public-exploit context, reported affected platforms, and defender hunts for CloudFiles registry symbolic links, suspicious wermgr.exe placement, and Windows Error Reporting task execution.

item.title: Telnyx PyPI TeamPCP compromise
item.description: OX Security reported malicious Telnyx Python SDK releases 4.87.1 and 4.87.2 uploaded to PyPI and attributed the activity to TeamPCP as a follow-on to LiteLLM. The page captures the reported _client.py payload, XOR-obfuscated WAV-like download stage, affected versions, Telnyx service-infrastructure caveat, and defender response guidance for developer and CI environments.

item.title: Developer-tool config auto-execution
item.description: SafeDep's June 2026 Miasma source-repository analysis shows repository-local configuration becoming a malware execution primitive: Claude Code and Gemini SessionStart hooks, Cursor alwaysApply rules, VS Code folderOpen tasks, and npm test scripts launched a large .github/setup.js dropper from poisoned GitHub repositories.

item.title: UNC3753
item.description: Mandiant / Google Threat Intelligence Group reports that UNC3753, also tracked as Luna Moth, Chatty Spider, and Silent Ransom Group, targeted dozens of U.S. legal, professional-services, and financial-services organizations from January through May 2026. The cluster uses invoice and data-migration pretexts, help-desk vishing, screen sharing, RMM tools, BYOD-to-VDI pivots, iManage/document-repository searches, WinSCP/Rclone/browser exfiltration, and rapid extortion sometimes within a single business day.

item.title: TeamPCP Python toolkit / FIRESCALE fallback analysis
item.description: Hunt.io analyzed a 13-file TeamPCP Python second-stage toolkit used after Mini Shai-Hulud-style supply-chain delivery. The update adds FIRESCALE GitHub commit-search fallback C2, victim-owned GitHub repository exfiltration, broad cloud/developer credential collection, AES-GCM/RSA-OAEP packaging, persistence/wiper sequencing, and infrastructure pivots including 83.142.209.194 and a Google Cloud fingerprint match.

item.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 exploitation
item.description: Cisco PSIRT says it became aware of exploitation of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 in June 2026. The authenticated CLI flaw can let a netadmin-level attacker upload a crafted file and execute commands as root; Cisco observed limited cases where exploitation pushed configuration changes to edge devices and had no direct fix or workaround at advisory version 1.2.

item.title: SolarWinds Serv-U CVE-2026-28318 exploitation
item.description: CISA added SolarWinds Serv-U CVE-2026-28318 to KEV on June 5, 2026. SolarWinds describes an unauthenticated denial-of-service flaw where specially crafted POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate can crash Serv-U 15.5.4 and below; fixed release is Serv-U 15.5.4 HF1.

item.title: Microsoft Claude Code Action runner-environment exposure case
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports a Claude Code GitHub Action case where prompt-injected GitHub issue or pull-request content could drive the agent Read tool to access /proc/self/environ, exposing the workflow ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and potentially other runner credentials despite Bash environment scrubbing. Microsoft says Anthropic mitigated the issue in Claude Code 2.1.128 by blocking sensitive /proc files.

item.title: Azure/durabletask repository reinfection in the Miasma / Phantom Gyp wave
item.description: StepSecurity reports a second compromise of the Azure/durabletask GitHub repository after the May 19 durabletask PyPI compromise. The June 5 malicious commit allegedly reused the same contributor account and planted Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code, and GitHub setup files that execute a 4.6 MB obfuscated credential-harvesting payload when the repository is opened in AI coding tools or VS Code.

item.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257 exploitation
item.description: Unit 42 confirms active exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 by an unidentified actor attempting to access GlobalProtect. Palo Alto Networks describes the issue as an authentication bypass in vulnerable GlobalProtect portal and gateway configurations that can establish unauthorized VPN connections; Unit 42 had not identified post-access behavior or lateral movement at publication time.

item.title: OP-512
item.description: ReliaQuest reports OP-512, a suspected new China-linked espionage cluster targeting legacy Microsoft IIS servers with a custom three-web-shell framework. The framework uses deployment-unique ASP.NET code, self-reporting hex-segmented DNS C2, and RSA+RC4-gated .ashx command handlers, making behavioral detections around w3wp.exe, unexpected ASP.NET compilation, and outbound DNS/HTTP more durable than static indicators.

item.title: Everest Forms Pro CVE-2026-3300 exploitation
item.description: The Hacker News reports active exploitation of Everest Forms Pro CVE-2026-3300, an unauthenticated PHP code-injection flaw in the Calculation Addon's process_filter() path affecting versions through 1.9.12. Wordfence-referenced telemetry says exploitation began April 13, 2026, with more than 29,300 blocked attempts and payloads creating a diksimarina administrator account.

item.title: PCPJack cloud SMTP relay network
item.description: Hunt.io reports that PCPJack infrastructure exposed a 12-file toolkit and Sliver working directory used to convert 230 compromised AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure Linux servers into a Chisel-backed SMTP relay network. SentinelOne separately describes PCPJack as a cloud credential-theft worm that removes TeamPCP-associated artifacts, so the wiki tracks the relationship as TeamPCP-adjacent rather than confirmed shared control.

item.title: Kali365 device-code phishing expansion
item.description: Arctic Wolf Labs reports that Kali365 expanded from Microsoft OAuth device-code phishing into a 126-host multi-brand phishing cluster impersonating Microsoft Outlook / Live, Okta SSO, Xerox DocuShare, AWS-themed services, GMX, Mail.ru, Odnoklassniki, Yandex Disk, and MAX Messenger while using live token-capture panel infrastructure under securehubcloud.com and phishing zones such as attachedfile.com.

item.title: TA4922
item.description: Proofpoint profiles TA4922 as a likely financially motivated Chinese-speaking cybercriminal cluster using localized HR, payroll, tax, invoicing, and business-process lures across East Asia, Europe, and Africa to deliver credential phishing, fraud paths, RMM tooling, ValleyRAT / Winos4.0, Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, and SilentRunLoader.

item.title: Claude Code GitHub Action prompt-injection boundary
item.description: GMO Flatt Security documents a Claude Code GitHub Actions trust-boundary flaw where untrusted GitHub issue or comment content could reach AI-agent workflows with repository, workflow, GitHub App, GITHUB_TOKEN, and OIDC privileges. Anthropic fixed the reported bypasses in claude-code-action v1.0.94; defenders should treat AI issue-triage workflows as untrusted input unless permissions and secrets are tightly scoped.

item.title: Stock exchange executive mailbox espionage
item.description: Broadcom / Symantec reports a five-month targeted espionage intrusion against a senior stock-exchange executive, focused on incremental Outlook mailbox theft through an Aspose-based OST-to-PST stealer, scheduled-task persistence, Dropbox API uploads, OneDrive Personal uploads through hard-coded Microsoft IP addresses, and masquerading Adobe, Lenovo, OneDrive, and Intel-themed paths.

item.title: Operation GriefLure Southeast Asia LNK dropper
item.description: Seqrite Labs reports Operation GriefLure, a Southeast Asia-focused spear-phishing campaign against Vietnam telecom and Philippine healthcare targets using authentic legal decoys, nested archives, Windows LNK files, ftp.exe living-off-the-land execution, runtime payload assembly from .doc chunks, sfsvc.exe and 360.dll loaders, explorer.exe process injection, HTTPS C2, credential theft, and moderate-to-high confidence China-nexus attribution.

item.title: binding.gyp npm CI/CD worm
item.description: StepSecurity reports the Miasma / Shai-Hulud-descended Phantom Gyp npm worm: 57 packages and 286+ malicious versions using binding.gyp/node-gyp install-time execution, Bun staging, GitHub Actions runner-memory secret scraping, GitHub dead-drop repositories under liuende501, AI-assistant/editor config backdoors, and npm/RubyGems propagation.

item.title: UNC6692 SNOW malware social-engineering campaign
item.description: Google Cloud / Mandiant reports that UNC6692 used Microsoft Teams helpdesk impersonation, fake mailbox-repair pages, attacker-controlled AWS S3 staging, AutoHotKey execution, the SNOWBELT malicious Chromium extension, SNOWGLAZE tunneling, and SNOWBASIN local command execution before internal scanning, PsExec, RDP to a backup server, LSASS dumping, and LimeWire exfiltration.

item.title: faster-axios / turbo-axios Epsilon Stealer npm campaign
item.description: SafeDep reports an npm typosquat campaign where turbo-axios and faster-axios copied the legitimate Axios source but added a postinstall loader that fetched remote JavaScript and delivered a Windows Epsilon Stealer payload with browser, wallet, Discord, Telegram, and GitHub 2FA-code theft, persistence, shellcode injection, and a WebSocket RAT channel.

item.title: IronWorm npm Rust infostealer campaign
item.description: JFrog Security Research reports IronWorm, a self-replicating npm supply-chain campaign that ships a native Linux Rust infostealer through preinstall, hides with an eBPF rootkit, uses Tor C2, harvests developer, cloud, AI, Kubernetes, package-registry, and wallet secrets, backdates malicious GitHub commits, and can use trusted-publishing OIDC flows to publish trojanized npm releases.

item.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer CVE-2026-45247 exploitation
item.description: CISA added Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer CVE-2026-45247 to KEV on June 3, 2026. Sansec, NVD, and Mirasvit reporting describe an unauthenticated PHP object-injection flaw in Magento / Adobe Commerce storefront traffic where a crafted CacheWarmer cookie reaches PHP unserialize and can lead to remote code execution before version 1.11.12.

item.title: Browser-based developer IDE OAuth token theft
item.description: Ammar Askar's June 2026 GitHub.dev / VS Code webview research shows how a browser-hosted developer IDE that receives broad source-control OAuth tokens can become a one-click token-theft surface. Defenders should treat browser IDEs as privileged developer applications, restrict extension installation, monitor OAuth and repository activity, and prefer scoped web-IDE tokens where platforms support them.

item.title: Agent skill marketplace poisoning
item.description: Trail of Bits reports bypasses against multiple AI-agent skill-scanning paths and warns that public skill marketplaces can distribute malicious skills that steal credentials, hide instructions in documents or bytecode, abuse prompt framing, or reconfigure package managers to attacker-controlled registries. The defender lesson is to treat skills as untrusted software-supply-chain dependencies, use curated catalogs, inspect full artifact trees, sandbox execution, and avoid trusting scanner pass results as an allow decision.

item.title: jqwik maintainer prompt-injection supply-chain pattern
item.description: Snyk reports that jqwik 1.10.0, a legitimate Maven Central release from the project maintainer, printed an ANSI-hidden prompt-injection instruction aimed at AI coding agents that ingest raw build and test output. The durable defender lesson is to treat process output from dependencies as untrusted data, strip terminal-control tricks, sandbox coding agents, and require explicit approval before destructive file operations.

item.title: MCP stdio command-execution boundary
item.description: OX Security reports a systemic Model Context Protocol trust-boundary pattern where user- or registry-controlled stdio server configuration can flow into subprocess execution through fields such as command and args. Defenders should treat MCP configuration as code execution, allow-list known servers, sandbox MCP subprocesses, and monitor AI-agent and developer-tool stdio launches.

item.title: Gamaredon GammaPhish / GammaWorm / GammaSteel chain
item.description: Sekoia reconstructs a January 2026 Gamaredon chain using WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 path traversal, Startup-folder HTA execution, GammaLoad VBScript staging, GammaWorm USB and network-share propagation, registry-backed dead-drop resolver configuration, and GammaSteel document theft from local, network, removable, and actively edited files.

item.title: Android Framework CVE-2025-48595 exploitation
item.description: CISA added Android Framework CVE-2025-48595 to KEV on June 2, 2026, and Google's June Android Security Bulletin says there are indications the integer-overflow privilege-escalation issue may be under limited, targeted exploitation.

item.title: Linux Kernel CVE-2022-0492 cgroup release_agent exploitation
item.description: CISA added Linux Kernel CVE-2022-0492 to KEV on June 2, 2026. The older cgroups v1 release_agent flaw can enable privilege escalation and namespace-isolation bypass under vulnerable kernel and container-host conditions.

item.title: Operation XENOFISCAL SideCopy XenoRAT campaign
item.description: Seqrite reports Operation XENOFISCAL, a SideCopy-attributed spear-phishing campaign targeting Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance provincial network with a Pashto .pdf.lnk lure, mshta remote HTA execution, obfuscated JavaScript and .NET loaders, registry persistence, in-memory shellcode execution, and XenoRAT 1.8.7 C2. Seqrite attributes the activity to SideCopy with medium-to-high confidence.

item.title: Operation FlutterBridge FlutterShell macOS malvertising
item.description: Unit 42 reports Operation FlutterBridge, a CL-CRI-1089 macOS malvertising campaign distributing signed and notarized FlutterShell applications through Google Ads and shell-company advertiser infrastructure. FlutterShell masquerades as podcast and PDF utilities while exposing WebView-driven backdoor primitives for command execution, file access, environment-variable extraction, browser hijacking, and possible AI-summarization data exfiltration.

item.title: WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732 exploitation
item.description: The Hacker News reports active exploitation of WP Maps Pro CVE-2026-8732, an unauthenticated WordPress plugin privilege-escalation flaw that can create administrator accounts through the wpgmp_temp_access_ajax path in versions up to and including 6.1.0. Wordfence-linked reporting cited 2,858 blocked attacks in 24 hours and a fixed 6.1.1 release.

item.title: Oracle WebLogic CVE-2024-21182 exploitation
item.description: CISA added CVE-2024-21182 to KEV on 2026-06-01. Oracle and NVD describe it as an unauthenticated, network-reachable WebLogic Server Core flaw over T3 and IIOP affecting 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0, with low exploit complexity and potential access to critical WebLogic-accessible data.

item.title: Operation Dragon Weave Azure Blob C2 campaign
item.description: Seqrite reports Operation Dragon Weave, a moderate-confidence China-linked espionage campaign targeting Czech Republic and Taiwan-linked victims with ZIP lures, dual LNK / Rust-dropper execution paths, RUSTCLOAK DLL sideloading, an AZUREVEIL Adaptix C2 payload, and Microsoft Azure Blob Storage dead-drop command and control.

item.title: Miasma RedHat Cloud Services npm wave
item.description: Wiz, StepSecurity, SafeDep, JFrog, OX, and Boost Security report Miasma, a Mini Shai-Hulud-derived wave compromising @redhat-cloud-services npm releases through malicious orphan GitHub commits, throwaway-branch GitHub Actions OIDC trusted publishing, valid provenance/SLSA attestations, preinstall execution, runner-memory secret extraction, bypass-2FA npm worming, three-wave publication, live-latest malicious releases during exposure, and GitHub repository dead drops with the description Miasma: The Spreading Blight.

item.title: Cloud Atlas PowerCloud / reverse-tunnel campaign
item.description: Kaspersky reports late-2025 and early-2026 Cloud Atlas espionage against Russia and Belarus government, diplomatic, and commercial targets, adding ZIP/LNK phishing, VBCloud, PowerShower, PowerCloud, reverse SSH, ReverseSocks, Tor hidden-service backup channels, RDP patching, and Google Sheets collection tradecraft.

item.title: Ghostwriter / FrostyNeighbor JavaScript PicassoLoader chain
item.description: ESET documents a March 2026 FrostyNeighbor / Ghostwriter campaign against Ukrainian government organizations using Ukrtelecom-themed PDF lures, server-side victim validation, RAR-delivered JavaScript, scheduled-task persistence, and a JavaScript PicassoLoader downloader for Cobalt Strike follow-on.

item.title: Famous Chollima Packagist dev-branch loader
item.description: Socket reports a Packagist-exposed roberts/leads dev branch with obfuscated JavaScript appended to tailwind.js, using blockchain and RPC dead drops to retrieve remote payloads in a targeted Famous Chollima / Contagious Interview-style developer lure.

item.title: PraisonAI CVE-2026-44338 rapid exploitation
item.description: Sysdig reports that internet-exposed PraisonAI agent-framework deployments were probed for CVE-2026-44338 less than four hours after advisory publication, validating unauthenticated GET /agents exposure and reinforcing that AI-agent API advisories can move to known-CVE scanner workflows within hours.

item.title: Dutch Police / NCSC 17-million-device botnet disruption
item.description: Dutch Police and NCSC-NL announced a disruption of an unnamed botnet with at least 17 million infected devices and 200 hosting / command servers in the Netherlands, emphasizing consumer, mobile, IoT, and edge-device exposure, residential-proxy abuse, and the need to treat takedowns as containment opportunities rather than endpoint cleanup.

item.title: OX details Shai-Hulud copycat npm packages
item.description: OX Security reports four npm typosquat packages from a non-TeamPCP copycat actor after the Shai-Hulud source-code leak, including chalk-tempalte as a near-direct clone, axios-themed stealers, a Phantom Bot DDoS package, lhr.life / IP-based C2 endpoints, and GitHub dead-drop strings defenders can hunt.

item.title: NATS-as-C2 KeyHunter credential-harvesting operation
item.description: Sysdig reports a Langflow CVE-2026-33017 intrusion where an actor harvested cloud credentials and attempted to enroll the host into a KeyHunter worker pool coordinated through authenticated NATS message-broker C2 with subject-level ACLs, JetStream-style tasking, AWS / AI-key validation, and code-sandbox secret scraping.

item.title: Microsoft details oob.moika.tech reconnaissance-first dependency-confusion cluster
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports a May 28-29 follow-up cluster of 33 malicious npm packages using oob.moika.tech infrastructure, internal-looking organizational scopes, spoofed enterprise metadata, postinstall stagers, CI bypass checks, cache deduplication, and reconnaissance-first profiling for possible selective follow-on exploitation.

item.title: Pirated media SilentCryptoMiner RAT campaign
item.description: Kaspersky reports an ongoing cybercrime campaign distributing a modified SilentCryptoMiner fork and RAT capability through fake plugin/update prompts on illegal movie, TV, and digital-library sites, combining DLL side-loading, UAC pressure, GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC service persistence, watchdog self-restoration, RAT C2, and XMRig-style mining.

item.title: Permiso ChatGPhish AI-summary phishing surface
item.description: Permiso reports ChatGPhish, a ChatGPT page-summarization rendering issue where attacker-controlled web-page content can become live Markdown links, auto-fetched remote images, spoofed system-style alerts, and QR-code phish inside the trusted assistant UI.

item.title: Marimo CVE-2026-39987 LLM-agent post-exploitation
item.description: Sysdig reports a May 2026 intrusion where an actor exploited marimo CVE-2026-39987, harvested cloud credentials, used Cloudflare Workers egress to retrieve an SSH key from AWS Secrets Manager, and used an LLM-agent-shaped command loop to dump an internal PostgreSQL database through a bastion.

item.title: GREYVIBE Russia-nexus AI-assisted Ukraine operations
item.description: WithSecure reports GREYVIBE as a Russia-nexus cluster targeting Ukraine and Ukraine-related entities with spear-phishing, ClickFix-style fake CAPTCHA pages, fake adult-club and drone-charity lures, PhantomRelay, FallSpy, LegionRelay, custom obfuscators, and systematic AI assistance across lures, infrastructure, malware development, and post-compromise scripts.

item.title: Socket details axios / plain-crypto-js RAT chain
item.description: Socket's technical analysis identifies axios@1.14.1 and axios@0.30.4 as suspicious npm publishes that pulled malicious plain-crypto-js@4.2.1 through a postinstall hook, delivered OS-specific RAT payloads from sfrclak.com, erased install-time evidence, and propagated into downstream vendored AI-tooling packages.

item.title: vpmdhaj OpenSearch npm cloud-secret stealer
item.description: Microsoft reports 14 malicious npm packages published by vpmdhaj that spoofed OpenSearch, Elasticsearch, DevOps, and environment-configuration tooling, executed through preinstall hooks, abused Bun runtime loading, and stole AWS, Vault, npm, GitHub Actions, and CI/CD secrets for cloud lateral movement and downstream package compromise.

item.title: Kimsuky / Emerald Sleet / TA427
item.description: Kaspersky and ENKI report that Kimsuky continues to expand PebbleDash and AppleSeed tooling, including HelloDoor, HttpMalice, HTTPSpy delivery chains, JSONPing infection checks, VS Code Remote Tunnel abuse, DWAgent, and Cloudflare Quick Tunnels against South Korean public, private, military, and corporate targets.

item.title: The Gentlemen ransomware
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports The Gentlemen as a Storm-2697-operated Windows RaaS encryptor written in Go and obfuscated with Garble, combining double extortion, Curve25519 / XChaCha20 per-file encryption, Defender and backup disruption, scheduled-task / Run-key persistence, and self-propagation across local drives and network shares.

item.title: StegaBin Pastebin-steganography npm campaign
item.description: Socket reports 26 malicious npm typosquats tied to North Korea's Contagious Interview activity using install scripts, obfuscated vendor/scrypt-js/version.js loaders, Pastebin character-level steganography, Vercel payload infrastructure, and a RAT that deploys nine developer-targeting infostealer modules.

item.title: BlackFile / UNC6671 vishing extortion operation
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports UNC6671 / BlackFile uses personal-phone vishing, AiTM SSO credential capture, attacker-controlled MFA-device registration, and SaaS data theft from Microsoft 365, Okta-connected applications, SharePoint, OneDrive, Zendesk, and Salesforce for extortion.

item.title: Sicoob.Sdk NuGet banking certificate stealer
item.description: Socket reports that malicious Sicoob.Sdk NuGet releases 2.0.0 through 2.0.4 impersonated an official Sicoob banking SDK, used a clean GitHub source façade, and exfiltrated client IDs, PFX passwords, base64-encoded PFX certificate archives, and boleto responses through a hardcoded Sentry endpoint.

item.title: Operation DangerousPassword axios npm compromise
item.description: ESET reports Lazarus Operation DangerousPassword activity compromised lead-maintainer credentials for the widely used axios JavaScript package and published malicious npm versions that injected trojanized code into downstream systems before detection and removal.

item.title: FortiClient EMS CVE-2026-35616 EKZ Infostealer campaign
item.description: Arctic Wolf reports May 2026 intrusions exploiting CVE-2026-35616 in FortiClient EMS to modify endpoint-management policy, execute PowerShell through FortiClient workflows, and deploy EKZ Infostealer disguised as FortiEndpoint_Patch.exe to harvest browser credentials, cookies, and autofill data from managed endpoints.

item.title: codexui-android OpenAI token stealer
item.description: Aikido Security reports that codexui-android, a legitimate-looking OpenAI Codex remote UI npm package with active development and about 27,000 weekly downloads, shipped npm-only code that read Codex auth.json tokens and posted access, refresh, and ID tokens to sentry.anyclaw.store/startlog; related Android apps bootstrapped the unpinned npm package on launch.

item.title: oob.moika.tech dependency-confusion environment stealer
item.description: SafeDep reports 164 npm dependency-confusion packages across cloud, ML, car-loan, deposit, and debit / internet-banking scopes; 162 active packages used postinstall execution to steal full environment variables, fetch detached second-stage scripts from oob.moika.tech, and disguise outbound activity as internal telemetry.

item.title: SafeDep live update on MicrosoftSystem64 / js-logger-pack
item.description: SafeDep reports the MicrosoftSystem64 payload remained active after earlier js-logger-pack disclosures, with a valid Hugging Face token, live C2, active victim screenshots and credential archives, version 1.0.8 Node SEA payload details, and a broader toskypi / jpeek identity cluster.

item.title: TeamPCP extortion ecosystem update
item.description: Unit 42 reports that TGR-CRI-1135 / TeamPCP has partnered with LAPSUS$ Group operators for data-leak-site extortion and with Vect ransomware operators or affiliates via BreachForums, while a claimed open-source Shai-Hulud release raises copycat and attribution-noise risk.

item.title: DAEMON Tools Lite supply-chain compromise
item.description: Kaspersky reports official DAEMON Tools Lite installers were trojanized from April 8 to May 5, 2026, with signed DTHelper.exe, DiscSoftBusServiceLite.exe, and DTShellHlp.exe backdoors contacting typosquatted infrastructure and selectively deploying an information collector, minimalistic backdoor, and QUIC RAT. CISA added CVE-2026-8398 to KEV on May 27.

item.title: Grandoreiro and BTMOB Latin America / Europe malware campaigns
item.description: WatchGuard, ESET, and The Hacker News report renewed Grandoreiro Windows banking-malware activity using phishing, DLL sideloading, and WebRTC/STUN/ICE communications camouflage, alongside BTMOB Android RAT-as-a-service activity with APK builders, Accessibility abuse, and ready-made regional lure tooling.

item.title: CISA adds Nx Console and TanStack supply-chain incidents to KEV
item.description: CISA's May 27 KEV catalog adds CVE-2026-48027 for Nx Console and CVE-2026-45321 for TanStack, validating active exploitation of trusted developer-channel compromises and setting June 10 remediation due dates for covered agencies.

item.title: Malware-Slop Claude user-data npm infostealer
item.description: OX Security reports Malware-Slop, a malicious npm package named mouse5212-super-formatter that used postinstall execution to exfiltrate Claude-associated /mnt/user-data files to actor-controlled GitHub repositories through the GitHub Contents API, falling back to a hardcoded leaked GitHub token.

item.title: JINX-0164 crypto developer infrastructure campaign
item.description: Wiz reports JINX-0164, a financially motivated actor targeting cryptocurrency organizations through LinkedIn social engineering, fake meeting and driver-fix pages, AUDIOFIX macOS malware, credential theft, internal repository poisoning, and the trojanized @velora-dex/sdk npm package delivering MINIRAT.

item.title: Glassworm developer supply-chain botnet
item.description: CrowdStrike reports a coordinated disruption of Glassworm, a developer-targeting supply-chain botnet that used malicious VS Code / OpenVSX extensions, npm and Python packages, poisoned GitHub repositories, GlassWormRAT, and resilient C2 via Solana dead drops, BitTorrent DHT, Google Calendar, and VPS infrastructure.

item.title: AI chatbot and SEO poisoning GPU-cryptojacking campaign
item.description: Microsoft reports an active cryptojacking campaign that impersonates trusted PC utilities, surfaces malicious download sites through search poisoning and observed AI chatbot recommendations, installs ScreenConnect for persistent access, hollows Microsoft-signed .NET utilities, and runs GPU miners from gleeze.com infrastructure.

item.title: Seedworm Dindoor / Fakeset U.S. network intrusions
item.description: Broadcom reports Seedworm access to a U.S. bank, airport, software supplier with Israeli operations, and U.S. / Canadian non-profits using the Dindoor Deno backdoor, Fakeset Python backdoor, signed certificates, Backblaze staging, and attempted Rclone exfiltration to Wasabi before the Iran-linked regional conflict widened.

item.title: Chinese-language PhaaS wallet-tokenization ecosystem
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports that Chinese-language phishing-as-a-service offerings have matured around RCS and iMessage lure delivery, live OTP interception through administration panels, and digital-wallet provisioning fraud that turns stolen payment data into attacker-controlled tokenized cards.

item.title: Fast16 nuclear-simulation sabotage framework
item.description: Broadcom / Symantec analyzed Fast16, a pre-Stuxnet sabotage framework that used a kernel file-system filter and rule-driven hooks to corrupt LS-DYNA and AUTODYN high-explosive / uranium-compression simulations associated with nuclear-weapon design, while spreading only inside target local networks.

item.title: forge-jsxy npm RAT
item.description: SafeDep reports that forge-jsxy continued the forge-jsx npm RAT campaign after takedown, shipping 22 versions through May 26 with keylogging, screenshots, wallet and Chromium-extension theft, durable persistence outside node_modules, WebRTC control, relay-pushed auto-upgrades, and exfiltration through 204.10.194.247, Discord, and Hugging Face.

item.title: Seedworm / MuddyWater signed-binary sideloading campaign
item.description: Broadcom reports a Q1 2026 Seedworm / MuddyWater espionage campaign across nine countries using Node.js-orchestrated PowerShell, signed Fortemedia and SentinelOne DLL sideloading, ChromElevator browser theft, SAM hive theft, SOCKS5 tunneling, and sendit.sh exfiltration.

item.title: Ababil of Minab MOIS-linked recovery-destruction campaign
item.description: Gambit Security links the Ababil of Minab persona to Iran MOIS-associated infrastructure and details a 2026 exfiltration and destructive campaign that targeted virtualization, storage, applications, and backup infrastructure to deny recovery across victims in the United States, Israel, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey.

item.title: SafeDep details AntV / atool Mini Shai-Hulud indicators
item.description: SafeDep's AntV / atool analysis adds Mini Shai-Hulud detection pivots: 637 malicious versions across 317 packages, payload hash and orphan antvis/G2 commit IDs, dual GitHub and OpenTelemetry-looking exfiltration, Docker-socket escape attempts, AI-assistant and VS Code persistence, kitty-monitor GitHub C2, and gh-token-monitor polling.

item.title: AI-augmented adversary operations
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports that adversaries are moving AI use into repeatable workflows for vulnerability discovery, exploit generation, obfuscation, autonomous malware operations, obfuscated model access, and AI software supply-chain initial access, including TeamPCP / UNC6780 activity against AI environments.

item.title: KnowledgeDeliver CVE-2026-5426 ViewState exploitation
item.description: Google Mandiant reports that KnowledgeDeliver deployments reused identical ASP.NET machineKey values, enabling CVE-2026-5426 ViewState deserialization RCE; an unknown actor deployed BLUEBEAM / Godzilla, tampered LMS JavaScript, and pushed visitors toward a fake plugin that installed Cobalt Strike Beacon.

item.title: Wiz details TeamPCP post-compromise cloud and GitHub abuse
item.description: Wiz CIRT reporting adds TeamPCP post-compromise tradecraft after supply-chain credential theft: live secret validation, AWS and ECS discovery, malicious GitHub workflow pull requests, workflow-log deletion, mass repository cloning, ECS Exec / SSM execution, and cloud/source-data exfiltration.

item.title: Funnull RingH23 and MacCMS supply-chain attacks
item.description: QiAnXin XLab reports that Funnull-linked activity resurfaced through compromised GoEdge / CDN management infrastructure, the RingH23 Linux toolkit, typosquatted CDN domains, and MacCMS upgrade-channel poisoning, enabling JavaScript injection, traffic hijacking, wallet replacement, Udev persistence, and LD_PRELOAD hiding across web supply-chain paths.

item.title: Mr_Rot13 cPanel CVE-2026-41940 backdoor campaign
item.description: QiAnXin XLab reports that Mr_Rot13 exploited cPanel / WHM CVE-2026-41940 to turn unauthenticated control-panel takeover into SSH-key persistence, PHP webshells, login-page credential theft, filemanager remote-control tooling, and long-lived hosting-node backdoors.

item.title: Polymarket npm wallet-drainer packages
item.description: SafeDep reports nine Polymarket-themed npm packages that used postinstall onboarding prompts, .env PRIVATE_KEY harvesting, Cloudflare Worker exfiltration, and AI-assistant-themed package names to steal Ethereum / Polygon wallet private keys from developers and traders.

item.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 ClickFix poisoning
item.description: QiAnXin XLab reports that attackers exploited Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 to steal Admin API keys, poison more than 700 Ghost sites with JavaScript loaders, and route visitors into FakeCaptcha / ClickFix malware delivery through cloaking infrastructure and evolving payload chains.

item.title: RemotePE memory-only Lazarus RAT
item.description: Fox-IT / NCC Group documented RemotePE, a Lazarus-linked memory-only RAT delivered by DPAPILoader and RemotePELoader with DPAPI environmental keying, ETW and userland-hook evasion, operator-controlled C2 delivery, and targeting of financial, cryptocurrency, and DeFi organizations.

item.title: Socket details SAP CAP / Cloud MTA Mini Shai-Hulud compromise
item.description: Socket's SAP CAP / Cloud MTA analysis adds affected package versions, Bun loader behavior, obfuscated execution.js payload details, enterprise developer reach, developer credential harvesting, and GitHub Actions runner-memory scraping to the Mini Shai-Hulud / TeamPCP-linked SAP wave.

item.title: TrapDoor crypto-stealer cross-ecosystem campaign
item.description: Socket reports TrapDoor, a supply-chain crypto-stealer campaign spanning npm, PyPI, and Crates.io packages that targets crypto, DeFi, AI, Solidity, Sui, and Move developers, with npm postinstall payloads, PyPI import-time remote JavaScript, Rust build.rs keystore theft, credential validation, SSH lateral movement, persistence, and AI-assistant instruction-file abuse.

item.title: js-logger-pack Hugging Face exfiltration campaign
item.description: JFrog reports that malicious js-logger-pack npm releases used Hugging Face both to distribute MicrosoftSystem64 Node SEA implants and to store stolen archives in attacker-controlled private datasets; affected developer or CI hosts should be treated as endpoint compromises.

item.title: ScarCruft Yanbian game-platform supply-chain attack
item.description: ESET reports that North Korea-aligned ScarCruft compromised a Yanbian-themed gaming platform, delivering RokRAT and BirdCall through Windows updates and Android BirdCall through trojanized mobile games used by a sensitive regional community.

item.title: APT28 LNK SmartScreen bypass and CVE-2026-32202 coercion chain
item.description: Akamai reports that an APT28 LNK exploit chain used CVE-2026-21513 and CVE-2026-21510 for SmartScreen bypass and remote code loading; patch analysis surfaced CVE-2026-32202, a residual zero-click authentication-coercion issue defenders should handle as a remaining forced-auth primitive.

item.title: Microsoft Defender CVE-2026-41091 / CVE-2026-45498 exploitation
item.description: CISA and Microsoft report active exploitation of Defender CVE-2026-41091 and CVE-2026-45498; defenders should verify Antimalware Platform updates to 1.1.26040.8 / 4.18.26040.7 or later and hunt for local privilege-escalation or Defender instability on lagging endpoints.

item.title: Trend Micro Apex One CVE-2026-34926 exploitation
item.description: CISA added Trend Micro Apex One CVE-2026-34926 to KEV after active exploitation; the on-premises server-side directory traversal issue can let an already-admin attacker inject code for deployment to managed agents.

item.title: Xinference PyPI compromise
item.description: JFrog reported legitimate xinference PyPI versions 2.6.0, 2.6.1, and 2.6.2 were compromised with import-time Python execution that collected developer, cloud, Kubernetes, and package-manager secrets and exfiltrated love.tar.gz to whereisitat.lucyatemysuperbox.space; TeamPCP attribution remains caveated after the persona denied involvement.

item.title: Snyk confirms Laravel-Lang all-version compromise posture
item.description: Snyk published Laravel-Lang advisories for lang, http-statuses, attributes, and actions, treating every version as affected, noting temporary Packagist unlisting, and reinforcing that fresh installs or updates after the tag-rewrite window should be handled as compromised until proven otherwise.

item.title: Laravel-Lang compromise expands to 700+ versions
item.description: Socket expanded Laravel-Lang compromise coverage to include laravel-lang/lang and roughly 700+ historical versions, with a Composer autoload.files RCE path, cross-platform PHP staging, DebugChromium.exe browser theft, and collectors for cloud, Kubernetes, Vault, CI/CD, password-manager, Git, VPN, and local secrets.

item.title: LiteSpeed cPanel CVE-2026-48172 active exploitation
item.description: LiteSpeed says CVE-2026-48172 is being actively exploited against the user-end cPanel plugin; any cPanel user can abuse lsws.redisAble / cpanel_jsonapi_func=redisAble to execute arbitrary scripts as root on affected shared-hosting nodes.

item.title: Ollama P2P cryptominer RAT campaign
item.description: Akamai reported a campaign abusing exposed Ollama /api/create endpoints to run shell downloaders and deploy vc, a custom Go P2P RAT and XMRig cryptominer dropper that stages in /dev/shm, masquerades as kworker, persists through cron, and routes mining traffic through libp2p.

item.title: Laravel-Lang Composer tag-rewrite compromise
item.description: StepSecurity reported a Laravel-Lang Composer supply-chain compromise where every tag across laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/actions, and laravel-lang/attributes was rewritten to malicious commits that used Composer autoload.files to fetch flipboxstudio.info payloads and exfiltrate CI/developer secrets.

item.title: BufferZoneCorp RubyGems / Go module CI poisoning
item.description: Socket reported a BufferZoneCorp cross-ecosystem package cluster where Ruby gems and Go modules used install-time execution, Go init hooks, GitHub Actions path/proxy tampering, credential theft, fake go wrappers, and SSH authorized_keys persistence against developer and CI environments.

item.title: GitHub / Packagist postinstall hook campaign
item.description: Socket reported a May 2026 cross-ecosystem supply-chain campaign where attacker-made GitHub commits added identical package.json postinstall hooks to Composer/Packagist projects, downloading gvfsd-network from GitHub Releases to /tmp/.sshd and executing it in the background.

item.title: Drupal Core CVE-2026-9082 active exploitation
item.description: CISA added Drupal Core CVE-2026-9082 to KEV; Akamai analysis describes a PostgreSQL-backed SQL-injection path through attacker-controlled PHP array keys reaching JSON:API, Views, Entity autocomplete, and related EntityQuery flows.

item.title: First VPN criminal infrastructure takedown
item.description: Eurojust, Europol, and FBI-sourced public reporting describe the May 2026 disruption of First VPN, a Russian-speaking forum-advertised criminal VPN/proxy service used for ransomware, fraud, data theft, scanning, and DDoS activity, with 33+ servers dismantled and 1vpns domains seized.

item.title: Ghostwriter UAC-0057 Prometheus-themed phishing
item.description: CERT-UA reports UAC-0057 / UNC1151 phishing against Ukrainian government organizations using compromised accounts, Prometheus certificate lures, OYSTERFRESH/OYSTERSHUCK/OYSTERBLUES JavaScript stages, registry persistence, Cloudflare-fronted .icu infrastructure, and possible Cobalt Strike follow-on.

item.title: Langflow CVE-2025-34291 active exploitation
item.description: CISA added Langflow CVE-2025-34291 to KEV after active exploitation; the browser-mediated origin-validation and token-refresh chain can expose AI-workflow credentials, with public reporting tying some exploitation to MuddyWater.

item.title: Megalodon GitHub Actions workflow backdooring
item.description: SafeDep and StepSecurity report 5,718 malicious commits across 5,561 GitHub repositories, adding SysDiag and Optimize-Build workflow backdoors that abuse weak branch protection, direct poisoned pipeline execution, CI OIDC, and outbound runner access to exfiltrate secrets to 216.126.225[.]129:8443.

item.title: Screening Serpens MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2 campaigns
item.description: Unit 42's May 2026 Screening Serpens report adds MiniUpdate, MiniJunk V2, AppDomainManager hijacking, DLL sideloading, recruitment lures, and U.S./Israel/UAE/Middle East targeting context for the Iran-nexus actor.

item.title: ROADtools Entra ID cloud-intrusion tradecraft
item.description: Unit 42's May 2026 ROADtools analysis ties the Entra ID toolkit to nation-state cloud intrusions, covering ROADrecon discovery, roadtx token exchange, device registration persistence, Microsoft Graph enumeration, and hunting heuristics.

item.title: LiteLLM TeamPCP PyPI compromise details
item.description: Boost Security Labs' TeamPCP LiteLLM analysis adds PyPI versions 1.82.7/1.82.8, Python .pth startup execution, models.litellm.cloud exfiltration, caveated Trivy bridge hypotheses, and GitHub repository exposure/destruction behavior.

item.title: Mini Shai-Hulud expands into Intercom Packagist artifact
item.description: Socket linked Intercom's PyPI-to-npm compromise chain to a malicious Packagist intercom/intercom-php@5.0.2 artifact that abused Composer plugin install/update hooks, mutable tag metadata, Bun download, and router_runtime.js-style credential theft.

item.title: npm token reset after Mini Shai-Hulud AntV wave
item.description: Socket reported that npm invalidated all granular write tokens that bypass 2FA after the AntV Mini Shai-Hulud burst; the reset disrupts stolen token reuse but does not fix workflow-level trusted-publishing and OIDC compromise paths.

item.title: Nx Console StepSecurity technical update
item.description: StepSecurity's expanded Nx Console analysis adds the orphan commit delivery path, hidden VS Code task, Bun runtime, multi-channel exfiltration, Sigstore/SLSA abuse logic, Python kitty-monitor persistence, and host/network indicators.

item.title: Showboat Linux post-exploitation framework
item.description: Lumen Black Lotus Labs disclosed Showboat, a Linux post-exploitation framework used against telecom targets with remote shell, file transfer, process hiding, persistence, SOCKS5 proxying, port mapping, and PRC-aligned infrastructure clustering.

item.title: GitHub Actions deployment poisoning
item.description: Boost Security Labs' deployment-poisoning research documents how fork pull requests can create or influence deployment metadata and trigger secret-bearing deployment_status workflows through command injection or attacker-controlled environment URLs.

item.title: node-ipc 2026 npm maintainer-account compromise
item.description: Socket and Snyk reporting on malicious node-ipc npm versions 9.1.6, 9.2.3, and 12.0.1, likely maintainer-account abuse, CommonJS module-load execution, and credential theft.

item.title: SANDWORM_MODE AI-toolchain npm worm
item.description: Socket's SANDWORM_MODE reporting adds a Shai-Hulud-style npm typosquat worm focused on CI secrets, git hook persistence, malicious GitHub Actions, MCP prompt-injection, and AI-toolchain credential theft.

item.description: Webworm 2025 activity adds Discord and Microsoft Graph C2 backdoors, GitHub staging, SoftEther VPN, and custom proxy chains across European and South African targets.
